  • .sr-only was deleted as "the same rule declared twice" without diffing the two — it carried padding:0; margin:-1px; border:0, which is the part of the visually-hidden recipe that stops a bordered element painting a 1px sliver. Restored.
  • ⚠️ The measurement baseline is auto-formatted by the command that precedes every commit. docs:reflow-comments --write reflowed eight mockup HTML files inside the same commit that reported the coverage number. Verified harmless — no class attribute changed — but nothing in the pipeline would have said otherwise.

🔴 AND THE GUARD RAIL THIS BRANCH DELETED IS BACK, LOUDER. portalCoverage's footer used to read "Done is when the remaining delta is mockup-only scaffolding — never when this reads 100%" — a previous session writing directly at whoever came next. It was rewritten because it "reads oddly at 100%", which is precisely when it was needed. Deleting a guard rail looks exactly like tidying prose, and no gate can tell the difference. It now states what the number cannot see — a dead branch, composition, reachability, whether a figure is true.

⚠️ AND THE AUDIT'S OWN CENTRAL THESIS WAS WRONG, CORRECTED BY HARKIRAT WITHIN THE HOUR. It read CLAUDE.md's "no longer a build-from specification" line and concluded that matching the mockup's composition was itself the error — an argument built from a document rather than from the person who set the direction. His answer: "the old design is essentially retired at this point. the design is the mockup." The line means the portal may be ahead of the sketchpad in places, not that following it is wrong. So the Armory regression is not "transplanting composition is a mistake" — the two add-chips were the right idea, and the defect was dropping a working keyboard shortcut while porting it. Port the design; keep what the portal already does better.

The instrument finally has a self-test. It grew this branch from a set comparison into eight heuristics — brace matching, five class-valued props, a 600-char declaration window, a one-hop helper lookup over a sibling corpus, a member call-graph with a keyword blacklist, a styled-class intersection — added one at a time, each raising the number, none tested. scripts/portalCoverage.test.mjs now proves every resolution path works and can fail, and is wired into npm test. Also fixed while there: npm run check walked nested node_modules, so a peer session's worktree turned the whole suite red for a reason unrelated to any code in it.

⚠️ One audit finding was retracted by Harkirat and the retraction taught more than the finding. The branch's size was raised as a risk — but he had said repeatedly not to push or PR, so its size is the direct consequence of his own standing decision. A harsh-audit framing rewards finding things, so anything unusual reads as a defect; "unusual, and not my call" must route to check whether this was chosen before it routes to report it. Noise in an audit devalues the real findings beside it.

🔴 AND THEN THE PAGE WAS FINALLY OPENED, AND ARMORY WAS DEAD. Every visit threw ReferenceError: data is not defined inside ArmoryRealm and stuck on the loading skeleton forever — a bare data where every other line already read load.data, copy-pasted from Broadcast's own const data = load.data binding that Armory never has. It has been in the tree since the commit that added the staged-count masthead figure, survived the harsh self-audit and the second audit that specifically went looking for exactly this class of bug, and every gate stayed green throughout, because portal:coverage/orphans/refs all scan source text and none of them execute it. Fixed to load.data.stagedUnknown/load.data.stagedOps. This is the harness-not-in-npm test item made concrete, not a new lesson — the same file's own comment already named the failure mode. With the crash cleared, the three items §16 flagged as unverified render correctly: the Armory New MP build / New DMZ build chips both announce their b/d keys, the Season StagedPanel's "Review & commit" is a real full-width .commit, and the composer's ComposePreview renders a Discord-shaped card once a name and a resolvable date are both entered. npm test still exits 0 after the fix.

🔴 AND THE FIRST FULL VISUAL SWEEP, WHICH IS THE THING THAT SHOULD HAVE HAPPENED FIRST. Every realm and every sub-view, opened and looked at, at 1280×880: Season's Track/Board/Repairs, Armory's Rack/Coverage/Compare/Bulk, Broadcast's Now-showing/Airtime, Access's By-admin/By-scope/Sessions, Analytics' Health/Usage/Timing/Reach/Search, Review, and Home. Desktop is the primary layout — Harkirat, mid-sweep: "desktop is the primary layout/device which the portal will be used on. Optimize it for desktop first. Mobile optimization is a future endeavour." Two real defects, both filed: a missing space in Armory Coverage's summary line (withthem), and Season's Board sub-view failing to mount at 375px — aria-pressed flips correctly, no console error fires, and the component simply never renders. Two false alarms resolved rather than filed: Armory Compare's "identical" columns measure evenly at 199.7px each (the 447-vs-567px figure does not reproduce), and a __peers() finding on a Weapon/Build/Category table is Broadcast's announcements grid behaving like a data table.

🔴 THE SEASON CLOCK'S FIVE HIERARCHY GAPS, CLOSED TWO DAYS AFTER THEY WERE WRITTEN DOWN. Attempt 13 was critiqued one hour after COMPANION §16.31 recorded it as settled, and the critique was never actioned in either codebase — the two records agreed only because they shipped in the same commit. One hero figure at clamp(56px,6.4vw,82px), alone in the face; the h:m:s demoted to one quiet mono line; real chips for the deadline labels, replacing a run-on string that orphaned RANKED onto its own row as though it were a third deadline; left-aligned, because it renders inside the masthead's LEFT column and was aligning its right edge to nothing; and an accent rule that closes the block and carries the tier, so the element that escalates is the element that terminates. The tiers no longer bump the hero's size — at 4× it is already the loudest thing on the masthead, and growing it further is the shouting the five-tier design exists to avoid.

⚠️ The clock rebuild almost shipped a silent regression in a file it never touched. home.js carried its own transcribed copy of the face markup, emitting .sc-u/.sc-sep independently — so rebuilding Season's face would have left Home's clock rendering against rules that no longer existed, a whole component reduced to unstyled inline text, with npm test, portal:orphans and portal:coverage all green because every one of them is a source scanner and the classes were still present. ClockFace is now exported from season.js and imported by Home; only the face is shared, because what surrounds it genuinely differs. ⚠️ ?today= does not travel this clock, despite the completion plan saying it does — countdownParts reads Date.now(), so date-travel changes which moment is selected and not the countdown. All five tiers were verified by setting data-tier and reading the computed styles back. ⚠️ And portal:orphans earned its keep inside the same change: the first version emitted .sc-t-n on every number, and it styled nothing.

🔴 AND THE GATE THAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT ALL OF IT. scripts/portalHarnessRender.test.js mounts all seven realms into a real document with preact's own render(), lets each useEffect fire, lets the harness stub resolve, and asserts the realm got past its skeleton. It is the first portal gate that executes a component rather than reading its source. Proved it can fail before it was trusted: the Armory data-undefined bug was reinstated, the gate exited 1 naming armory alone, and it was reverted — a gate that has never failed is not known to work.

⚠️ It could not be an SSR test, which is the non-obvious part. Every realm loads through useAsync, and useAsync fetches inside a useEffect; preact-render-to-string does not run effects, so an SSR render of any realm reaches the loading skeleton and stops — the loaded branch, where all three known instances of this bug class lived, is never evaluated. linkedom is now a devDependency for exactly this. ⚠️ And a non-empty tree is not the assertion: a realm whose loader failed still renders the shell and a skeleton, which is a perfectly valid non-empty tree and is precisely what the dead Armory looked like for a day. The check requires the masthead, and collects preact's _catchError path, uncaughtException, unhandledRejection and console.error, because a component that throws during render does not reliably reject a promise. ⚠️ It is not scripts/portalHarness.test.js, which already existed and checks the stub's payload shape while rendering no component.

🔴 THE PORTAL STAGES FROM SIX REALMS AND ACKNOWLEDGED IT NOWHERE BUT A TOAST. .count-bump and .staged-pulse have had rules in the adopted stylesheet since it was adopted, and nothing has ever applied either — the mockup applies them from Shell.pulseTray() and that half was never ported. It is ported now, into shell.js (the module that owns both targets) and called from one place: composeClient.js's stageOps, the single funnel every staging path goes through, which is exactly why the mockup put its own call inside Store.add. ⚠️ Only on a real stage — a refusal, an expired session and a validation failure all return through that same call. Verified in the browser both ways: a real stage bumps the badge with the real countBump animation, an injected ?fail=/api/changeset bumps nothing.

⚠️ The badge could not simply be bumped when the stage returns, and the first two attempts were both wrong. The mockup's store is synchronous, so its count is already updated when it pulses; here a stage is a round trip plus a refetch plus a re-render, and at 0→1 the badge node does not exist yet. Waiting for the count to change was the second wrong answer — staging into an existing changeset adds an op and leaves the count alone, a real case that trigger would never have fired for, silently.

🟢 And two of the four "missing" interactions were never missing. .lift/.tint are applied by selector, which app.css's own block states in capitals as the decision — measured on the live page, Armory's rack cards lift and tint through their own component rule. A tracker reading class NAMES reports absence for a behaviour that is present. ⚠️ One real defect did fall out of measuring it: .wcard sits in the enumerated card list in both codebases and is emitted by nothing in either — a name transcribed from the mockup for a component the portal calls something else, the .stat.live shape again.

🔴 AND THE HARNESS COULD NOT STAGE AT ALL, WHICH ONLY WIRING THE ACKNOWLEDGEMENT REVEALED. /api/changeset is a GET that lists and a POST that stages, and the stub answered both with the list body — so every POST came back with no changesetId. Nothing rendered wrong, which is why it survived: stageOps ignores the body. But stageAndCommit reads staged.changesetId and takes its "Could not stage the change." branch without it, so the Manifest's inline edit reported failure on every save in the harness. ⚠️ portalHarness.test.js could not see it either — it compares the keys a stub returns against the keys the route promises, and a path registered once for two methods has one set of keys to compare against.

🔴 AND THE ARMORY LIVE PREVIEW SHOWED THE SAME CARD FOR EVERY BUILD — a defect that RENDERS, looks right, and is about a different weapon. The panel's whole claim is that it is what Discord will send for the record beside it. The raw Armory fixtures carry id, not _id (armoryBuild() is what normalises them), and the stub's /api/armory/preview searched the un-normalised array — so String(b._id) was the literal string "undefined" for every build, matched the real id the component sends for none of them, and every row fell through to the generic AK-47 fallback card. Opening .50 GS and reading AK-47 · Best AR · 6ZQ4-KP2M-VX90 beside it is the only thing that could have said so; the tracker had this item at half-proven, and half was the wrong half. Now verified across two different rows: the card follows the editor.

🟢 AND THE PLAYLIST DENSITY PLOT WAS APPROVED, THEN FOUND ALREADY BUILT. Harkirat's answer in the batched pop-up round was "build the density plot" — and track.js already samples concurrency at 64 points across the visible window, scales it gamma-0.6 (a linear height renders six bars in seven as a 14% stub), draws empty days explicitly rather than erasing them, and derives "7 at peak" from the curve's own max. Measured live: 64 bars, 14 zero-days drawn, the peak text right. The entry had read paused pending the Preact migration, and the migration is what built it. That is §0's failure mode for the third time in one session — a record describing as pending something that had already shipped.

🔴 PER-REALM COMPOSITION — ARMORY, ANALYTICS AND REVIEW, EACH AGAINST THE MOCKUP RATHER THAN AGAINST AN OPINION. The completion plan calls Armory's board a panel on the page rather than the page and Analytics a generic dashboard: four tiles above two panels. Both were measured before anything was changed, and the measurement is what the fixes are shaped around.

⚠️ ARMORY: 340 × 7,725 PIXELS OF THE REALM'S PRIMARY SURFACE WERE RESERVED FOR ONE SENTENCE. The bed grid was 798px 340px, and the second column's entire content was "Click a row below to open it." — down the whole height of the rack. The editor carries its own preview column inside the main cell, so the outer aside was never going to hold anything else. The empty cell is dropped now and the board runs the full 1,158px the mockup gives it, +45% width; the hint moved into the flow above the Manifest, which is where the clickable rows actually are. ⚠️ And the masthead counted builds twice — as the lead figure and again three columns right, reading as two measurements that happen to agree. It now reads 133 builds · 70 weapons · 66 need repair · 106 stale · 1 staged: the faults-versus-age split Coverage's own headline has always made in words ("66 builds have something actually wrong with them, and 106 more are merely old"), made by the figures too, both reading from splitCoverage so they cannot disagree. The old single flagged read 117 of 133 — a number close enough to the total to say nothing — because it counted "not touched in 90 days" as a defect.

⚠️ ANALYTICS: THE TILES SAID WHAT THE MASTHEAD HAD JUST SAID. Measured: masthead uptime 1h 30m · errors 24h 23 · commands 24h 496, and three of the four tiles beneath it repeated those three figures verbatim. That is why the page read as a generic dashboard — the tiles were not a second layer, they were the first one again. Each tile now carries something the masthead cannot, and every one of them was already on the page in a weaker position: Restarts 7d was a sentence inside a panel, Distinct users 24h and Quiet alerts 24h were sub-lines under figures they were not about. The quiet count is deliberately its own figure rather than small print under the red one — this repo's three-tier error model must never collapse into one number, and a caution that only exists as a footnote has collapsed. Verified: zero overlap between masthead and tiles.

⚠️ REVIEW: THE MASTHEAD COUNTED EVERY BLOCKER AND THE FOOTER NAMED ONE. blockersFor returns a list — an export gate, a stale record, a failed validation, one entry per unconfirmed tier-3 changeset — and the gate rendered blockers[0] only. On the fixture the masthead read BLOCKERS 3 above a single sentence, so a reader who cleared that one had no way to learn what the other two were except by pressing Commit and being refused again. All three are listed now, each with its own way through where one exists — which is what the comment directly above that code had already committed to for the export case. ⚠️ Review's composition was otherwise left alone deliberately: it is AHEAD of the mockup (typed confirmation, a real export gate, per-op transactions), and the mockup's own sample data renders [object Object] in four places.

🔴 THE SEASON RECORD'S THREE BANNERS WERE PICTURES RENDERED AS A SENTENCE ABOUT A PICTURE. Three of the record's six cells are images, and each read "image cached and serving" — which makes them scan as three more deadlines with unusually wordy values, and asserts the one thing a reader would rather just see. They render as real thumbnails now, in the same grid cell the sentence occupied, so the six cells stay peers rather than splitting into two designs. The picture is what distinguishes a banner from a deadline by KIND instead of by reading the label.

🔴 AND IT IMMEDIATELY FOUND THAT TWO OF THE THREE LIVE BANNERS ARE DEAD. Both are media.discordapp.net links carrying an expired ex= signature, so they render as nothing in Discord too — the record now says "set, but the image will not load" in the warn voice, which is a third state between "no image set" and a served one. Nothing could see this before: the status sentence said "cached and serving" for a stored URL whether or not anything was at the other end of it.

⚠️ THE RE-HOSTING HARKIRAT ASKED FOR IS ALREADY BUILT — one stable public id per banner, a new upload overwriting the previous one, exactly three assets ever. utils/calendarBannerCache.js's publicIdFor(page) is calendar_banners/draws|events|playlists with overwrite:true, invalidate:true, and both write paths go through it: /manage's Calendar handler and the portal's own calendar.setBanners op. The Discord-CDN skip was reverted on 2026-08-07 for precisely this reason, and that file's comment predicted the exact rows now showing dead: "only exists for pre-2026-08-07 DB rows that haven't been re-saved yet." The mechanism was never the gap — the gap was that nothing told anybody which rows still needed re-saving, and the source URLs are long expired so no script can repair them. Re-pasting a URL in the record's editor, three fields down from the warning, is the repair, and it re-hosts permanently.

🔴 THE RECORD'S CLOSE TARGET COLLAPSED FROM 147px TO 52px THE MOMENT IT OPENED. Collapsed, the whole strip is click-anywhere; open, the only way back was the Done button at the far right — same y-position, a fraction of the area. Harkirat's call: the header's empty space closes it. ⚠️ Not role="button" on the header — it contains the Live/Next switch and Done, and an interactive element wrapping other interactive elements is invalid ARIA and unusable from a keyboard; the keyboard path is still Done, and this adds the pointer target that was missing. ⚠️ The handler tests its own event target rather than relying on stopPropagation at each child, so a control added to that row later cannot silently start closing the panel. Verified both ways: the empty space closes it, the scope switch does not.

⚠️ The expanded editor panel was MEASURED before it was judged, which is the whole point of that item. compact-I's confession was "I called it 'fine' three times and never measured it once." Measured: 1,112 × 602, field rows aligned on a consistent label and input axis, the only flagged spread being different row TYPES rather than a drift. It is fine — and now that is a reading rather than an impression.

🔴 HOME STATED THE STAGED COUNT THREE TIMES INSIDE 500 PIXELS — the masthead figure, an entry on the attention list, and the staged bar sixteen pixels below that entry saying the same sentence with more in it (the realm breakdown, and the button that acts on it). COMPANION §16.6 warns about this exact shape: "a third copy of a fact stated above it." The list entry is gone, and dropping it corrected the lead figure: that list is EXCEPTIONS, needs you counts its rows, and staged work is not wrong — it is pending — so counting it there inflated the one number the page is named after by conflating a problem with a queue. It reads 3 now, beside a staged 4 in its own voice.

⚠️ And Home was missing a masthead figure the plan names. §5.9z.5 specifies four — days left · live now · staged · needs you — and the built version carried three. days left is the figure a person opening the console first actually acts on, and Home was the only realm not saying it. It reads from seasonMoments, the same derivation Home's own clock uses, so the two cannot disagree, and is absent rather than guessed when no deadline is set. Home now reads needs you 3 · days left 14 · live now 2 · staged 4.

🔴 AND THE SESSION'S LAST FINDING EXPLAINS WHY THE PORTAL'S "WHAT REMAINS" QUESTION HAD BEEN UNANSWERABLE FOR WEEKS. Every handoff, the canonical docs/reference/session-handoff-guide.md, MEMORY.md's own index line and the completion plan all asserted that no search reaches local/handoff/ — one of them spelling it out as "not rg, not --hidden, not -uu". Measured 2026-08-27 13:50 EDT on a phrase that exists only in a handoff: a default rg returns 0, --hidden returns 0, and rg -uu returns 1. local/ is gitignored, not hidden; --hidden only lifts the dotfile filter, so the claim generalised from the flag that fails to the one that works. Corrected in the guide, the plan, the memory index and reference_handoff_file_location.md.

⚠️ THE CORRECT RULE WAS NEVER MISSING, AND THAT IS THE ACTUAL LESSON. ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md is auto-loaded into every session, states the flag rule with its own measurement, and names local/ explicitly; usage-guard.mjs fires the same advice as a live hook and fired it repeatedly during the session that finally caught this. The repo-local claim won anyway, for months, across ~17 documents. A false SPECIFIC claim beats a true GENERAL rule because it is camouflaged as an exception to it — "these particular files are unreachable" reads as domain knowledge from someone who checked, not as a contradiction, so the general rule is left intact and quietly overridden. 🔴 When a document says a rule you already hold does not apply here, test the EXCEPTION rather than the rule — it is the higher-variance claim and this one cost a single command. And repetition is not corroboration: seventeen copies of one untested sentence is one source. Filed as the memory feedback_false_tool_reach_claims.

🔴 The cost was concrete. Told the exhaustive records were unsearchable, sessions did not search them, so every residual list was assembled from the tracked subset and came back confidently incomplete — five design items existed only there, and locating the gap took three forced sequentialthinking passes at Harkirat's insistence. A false claim about a tool's reach is self-sealing: acting on it produces exactly the evidence that confirms it.

🔴 AND THE HANDOFF WAS READER-TESTED AGAINST THE FILESYSTEM, WHICH FOUND TWO BLOCKERS IN A DOCUMENT WRITTEN BY THE SESSION THAT HAD JUST SPENT THE DAY FIXING THIS EXACT DEFECT CLASS. The worst was perfect in its irony: §0's headline measurement quoted a probe phrase, and writing the correction down put that phrase into two tracked files — so within the hour a default rg returned 2 where the table promised 0. A reader doing exactly what the section trains them to do — test the claim — would have seen it refuted and concluded the opposite of the truth. A probe quoted in a tracked document stops being a valid probe; it is replaced by a command plus an invariant SHAPE (0 · 0 · non-zero), with the probe declared disposable and the reason stated. The second blocker was two different counts of the same thing inside one file, reconciling with neither reality — replaced by the structural rule, which needs no maintenance.

⚠️ Thirteen more findings, all fixed. A..B excludes A, so the stated commit range returned nine of the ten rows it promised · npm run <script> --write silently swallows the flag and runs --check, looping the reader · the open-work table was not the whole open list (both the tracked deferred list and the previous handoff's own still-open rows carried items), so it gained a Filed? column and now names them · section references carried no paths, in a document whose entire thesis is findability · a boot command's prerequisites were unstated and it wrongly read as blocked on Harkirat · and the repo-root CLAUDE.md contradicted the handoff about ?today=, which matters more than an ordinary disagreement because the auto-loaded file is the one that wins. Corrected at source in CLAUDE.md, in the plan's status stamp, and in a stale scripts/buildPortal.js comment that named the wrong launch config for the very page it tells you to open first.

✅ docs/reference/session-handoff-guide.md gained §3b — the seven ways a handoff misleads a reader who TRUSTS it, each with the convention that prevents it, plus a third boolean (filed?) and a mandatory filesystem-verified reader test in its own "how to know it is DONE" checks. The reader test is not polish — it is the step that catches what care does not.

⚠️ RUNNING TEXT HAD NO MEASURE ON FIVE SELECTORS, AND THE STYLESHEET ALREADY HAD THE CONVENTION. .masthead p caps at 78ch, .failbox p at 70ch, .hmast p at 56ch, .rvnone p at 46ch and .estate p at 44ch — prose is capped everywhere this file thought about it. .racknote, .chint, .hint, .nodraft p and .hbanner p were never capped, and measured at 1700px — the width Arc with its side tab bar actually gives the page — they ran to 180–193 characters per line, roughly double a comfortable measure. Capped at 78ch, the most generous figure already in the file, so nothing narrows past a line already considered acceptable. ⚠️ .callout is deliberately excluded: it carries a tint and a 3px left border, so it is a BOX, and capping it leaves a 625px tinted panel floating in a 1534px one — a layout fault dressed as a measure. Its long line is a known, accepted cost.

✅ The 1700px pass otherwise came back clean — no horizontal overflow on any of the seven routes, every realm mounts, no orphaned right gap. That width had never been checked before.

⚠️ And a rendered typo, from a line break inside a template literal. Coverage read "something actually wrong withthem" — htm collapses a whitespace run containing a newline to nothing at an expression boundary, so breaking the line after with deleted the space. The space now lives inside the string, with the reason beside it.

🔴 ARMORY TAKES THE MOCKUP'S VOCABULARY AND ITS MODE SWITCH — Harkirat's call, made by looking rather than by reading. The choice had been deferred twice as "vocabulary, not composition." It was settled by publishing the live view bar and the mockup's version as two pixel-aligned renders of the same running page — the second produced by applying the changes to the DOM and re-photographing it, so the type, spacing and colour were the portal's own — and flipping between them. "the mockups version is better." The views are now Tier board · Repairs · Compare · Bulk & export, and Repairs earns it outright: Coverage named a measurement, Repairs names what you came to do, and Season already calls the same idea by that word.

🔴 AND THE MODE TURNED OUT TO BE THE REAL FINDING: IT WAS A PROPERTY OF ONE PANEL. MP/DMZ lived as BulkView's private state, so the Bulk view quietly filtered to one armory while the Rack, Repairs and Compare showed both mixed together and the masthead totalled them — five figures describing a population no view was displaying. MP and DMZ are two armories with different rules (DMZ has no share code and ranks by combat range), so the switch now sits in the view bar ahead of the views, and every figure and every view reads from it. Measured live: MP 125 builds · 68 weapons · 60 need repair · 106 stale; DMZ 8 · 7 · 6 · 0 — and the two halves add up to the old totals exactly, which is the check that the split lost nothing. BulkView's own switch is gone: two controls over one quantity can disagree, and that is the defect this branch keeps finding rather than a harmless duplicate.

⚠️ The four view names now live in ONE table. They were bare literals in five places, which is precisely how a rename becomes a silent dead branch — view === 'Rack' against a strip offering Tier board compiles, runs, and renders the fallback view forever.

✅ The realm key names only states that are ON SCREEN, which is the one thing a hardcoded legend cannot do. Switch to DMZ and stale disappears from the key, because DMZ has none — verified live — so the key can never send a reader hunting for a mark the page is not drawing. clean is drawn as an empty slot rather than a colour: a clean build carries no mark at all, and inventing a green swatch would teach a mark the portal does not use. It sits beside the shared state key, which explains SHAPE for every realm; a realm key explains only marks that realm draws.

(The code for all four of the above landed in 6304122, which carried the prose-measure fix in the same commit.)

🔴 THE PORTAL DECLARED TWO TYPEFACES IT NEVER LOADED, AND EVERY LARGE NUMBER IN THE CONSOLE WAS RENDERING IN THE BODY FACE. --display asks for Big Shoulders Display and --title for Instrument Serif; the font link requested only Space Grotesk and JetBrains Mono. So --display fell through to Space Grotesk on all seven rules that use it — every masthead h1, every masthead figure, the Analytics tiles, Home's h1, the header commit chip, the season clock's face and the health columns — and --title fell through to Georgia, putting the only serif in the entire console on the season record's title. The mockups load all four faces; the portal loaded two. ⚠️ COMPANION already records this exact bug once — "the portal declared Space Grotesk and JetBrains Mono and loaded neither" — it was fixed for those two and two more faces were left behind, which is failure mode #5 again: a per-case fix that leaves its siblings wrong.

🔴 AND THE FALSIFIER IS WHY THIS IS A MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN A CLAIM, because "the link now lists it" is not evidence a face arrived. Render one string in var(--ui) and in var(--display) and compare: two different faces cannot measure identically. Before: 444px and 444px. After: 441px, 324px and 315px across --ui, --display and --title — three distinct faces, and document.fonts reports both new families loaded. It is the same falsifier the first font bug was caught with, which is exactly why it should have been re-run when a third and fourth face were declared.

🔴 THE EXPORT STRIP SAT FLUSH AGAINST THE WINDOW EDGE BECAUSE THREE OF ITS DECLARATIONS WERE INERT. .mh-take read grid-column:2; grid-row:3; justify-self:end — grid-placement properties — and the strip had been moved out of .masthead into <main>, which is display:block. All three silently no-opped, so 4 formats rendered hard against the frame while every panel below stopped 22px short: measured strip right 1280, panel right 1258. It now aligns by a mechanism that applies to a block child, against a new --edge token naming that inset, and measures 1258 = 1258 on every realm that has one.

🔴 SEASON'S MASTHEAD STATED TWO OF ITS THREE EYEBROW FIGURES TWICE, AND ITS BIGGEST NUMBER THREE TIMES. The eyebrow read 14 LIVE NOW · 4 STAGED · 2 FLAGS above the title while the stats row on the far side of the same masthead read DAYS LEFT 14 · DRAWS LIVE 14 · STAGED 4 — and the 82px clock directly beneath both said 14 DAYS LEFT a third time. flags was the only figure the eyebrow alone carried, so it moved into the stats row and the eyebrow was deleted with its CSS; days left left the stats row, because the clock is the largest thing on the page and a 34px copy of it is a second authority over one quantity. Home keeps days left as a figure precisely because Home has no clock. Season now reads 14 draws live · 2 flags · 4 staged.

✅ AND /api/analytics IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: 42.1 KB, against a 495 KB baseline and a verify condition of under 100 KB. The tracker's remedy — "move the three text exports behind their own route" — had been overtaken: 38c7ec6 deleted them from the payload outright, and it landed 2h20m after the 495 KB reading was taken, so the row was stale rather than open. What was genuinely missing was the verification, which needs a real boot. Run against the dev database through the route's own functions: river 37.4 KB of the 42.1 (100 items, bounded per collection), everything else under 2 KB. The portal server also boots clean against Mongo and 401s the API without a session.

🔴 SEASON'S MASTHEAD WAS REBUILT AGAINST THE APPROVED DESIGN, AND THE FIRST ATTEMPT AT IT THIS SESSION CUT THE WRONG END. The duplication was real — 14 LIVE NOW · 4 STAGED above the title, DRAWS LIVE 14 · STAGED 4 in the stats row on the far side of the same masthead — and the first fix deleted the eyebrow. COMPANION §16.31 point 3 says the opposite in as many words: the clock "replaces the masthead's stat block, which he called useless. LIVE NOW / STAGED / FLAGS demote to an eyebrow above the page title." The stat block is the half that should not exist. So the eyebrow is restored, Season has no stats row at all, and the clock moved into the grid area the stat block occupied — which is what "replaces" means in a layout rather than only in prose. 🔴 A redundancy has two ends and which one to cut is a design decision somebody already made. Its internal form is unchanged: §16.31a's five hierarchy gaps were about the text inside the clock being ragged, not about which column it lives in.

✅ And the masthead's sub-line was showing a date range where the design has prose. It read 2026-08-06 → 2026-09-19 — which is the season record's job, three inches below, and §16.32 is explicit that the record shows the dates as stored. It now reads what the mockup writes: "Everything scheduled this season on one axis — and whether it still fits inside the season's own deadlines."

🔴 THE CALENDAR HAS THREE CATEGORIES AND THE PORTAL KNEW ABOUT TWO, SO DRAW WINDOWS RENDERED AS EVENTS. utils/adminParser.js accepts draw, event and playlist; every Season surface special-cased playlist and let everything else fall through to Event. A calendar row with category draw — a draw window, i.e. when a draw can actually be bought — drew in the Events lane, in the Events colour, and the Manifest called it an Event. That is precisely the defect the playlist split was written to fix, stopped one category short: its own comment says a playlist "rendered in the Events lane in the Events colour", and the fix that removed it left the third category doing the same thing. Replaced with one CAL_CATEGORY table that decides lane, label and topic colour together, so a fourth category cannot silently mean "event" again.

✅ Which made the sixth create control real rather than cosmetic. The mockup's ADD row has six chips and the portal had five; the missing one was Draw window, and it turned out the portal could always store one — fixtures.js declares its source as calendar category:'draw' and it maps to calendar.add, the same op Event and Playlist use. It never offered the control, so the one calendar category of three a person could not create was the one the Track draws a lane for. ⚠️ And buildSeasonAddOp would have filed it as an Event: the category read fields.category || (kind === 'playlist' ? 'Playlist' : 'Event'), the exact shape that once staged a patch note as a calendar event. It is a lookup now, and an unknown kind throws by name instead of defaulting. New topic accent --dw at hue ~307°, chosen to sit in the widest gap of the existing wheel so the set's tightest hue gap stays where it was; the mockup's own #6B4E7D is the right family and measures 2.86:1 under near-black, and these accents are bar fills.

✅ Two smaller things the mockup states and the portal did not. The ADD row announces its N shortcut as a visible kbd (the rule MastheadNew already followed), bound through useCreateKey so it cannot fire while somebody is typing a title. And the export strip's summary read 4 formats — how many buttons are behind the control, and nothing about what you would get. It now leads with the data: 39 items · 4 formats, summed from counts every scope already carried and left unused. Progress still replaces inventory once anything has been taken.

🔴 THREE OF THE SIX REALMS HAD NO WAY TO GET THEIR DATA OUT, AND NOBODY HAD NOTICED BECAUSE NOTHING COMPARED THE REALMS TO EACH OTHER. CLAUDE.md describes the Export strip as something the shell mounts on every realm; measured, only Season and Armory passed exports=, and /api/broadcast/export, /api/access/export and /api/analytics/export did not exist at all. Found by extracting a structured inventory from the running portal and from the mockup pages and diffing them — two evaluate_script calls for all thirteen pages, instead of the screenshot-and-eyeball loop that had been costing six turns per finding.

🔴 The two most valuable exports were the two missing ones. An announcement's text is the whole artifact — written once, stored nowhere else, derivable from nothing — and AdminUser is the only record of who can do what, on a page that is owner-only. Broadcast gets live and all as readable blocks; Access gets admins as blocks and the permission grid as CSV, because flattening a grid to prose loses the direct-vs-inherited distinction that is the entire reason a grid beats a comma-separated string. Neither is re-importable and both say so: there is no bulk-add flow for either, and a note promising a round trip would be a false claim about the file.

✅ Analytics exports TABLES, not the bot's prose. /bot analytics already hands a person a readable .txt in Discord, and this branch deliberately deleted those three text builds from the page payload — but the mockup's own strip offers "CSV for a spreadsheet", which is a different artifact for a different act: reading versus pivoting. Five tables, one per panel the dashboard draws, each re-querying on download so an export taken later is the data as it is then rather than a snapshot of a stale tab.

🔴 AND THE COLUMNS WERE WRITTEN FROM THE DASHBOARD'S VOCABULARY, SO FOUR OF THE FIVE WERE WRONG. Checked against the real dev database before shipping rather than after: computeUsageStats returns an object whose rows live under byCommand as {_id, c, ok, bg}, timing's are {_id, p, n} with p a raw sample array, reach rows are {context, installType, n}, and the river is a union of three collections. A getter naming a field nobody returns produces an empty column, not an error — five tidy CSVs with blank data look exactly like five correct ones. Verified per scope with a filled-cell count: events 6/6 · usage 4/4 · timing 4/4 · reach 3/3 · searches 6/6, every one against live rows. The same check caught the Access matrix reaching for a top-level m.grants[id] that does not exist, which would have written a spreadsheet asserting nobody holds anything.

⚠️ Three gates refused this change and all three were right on the merits, not merely mechanically. The export-scope gate rejected a csvScope() factory because it fills unit and filename uniformly — which is exactly what "each scope states its own shape" exists to prevent, and the gate reads these as source literals so a helper is invisible to it. The harness gate then failed on all three new routes at once, because scripts/lib/portalRouteQuery.js drives a route with a bare path unless it is registered there, and an export with no scope answers 400. A new export cannot be added in one place, by design.

✅ Measured after: Season 39 items · 4 formats — the mockup's own line, exactly — plus Armory 133 · 2, Broadcast 6 · 2, Access 8 · 3, Analytics 32 · 5. Review and Home have none, which is also what the mockup draws.

✅ Four Armory labels named things the columns do not contain, and one named a view that no longer exists. Runs was the attachments cell — five named parts, not a usage count nobody stores; Code is the bot's gunsmith code everywhere else it appears; the rack panel's eyebrow still read Rack — by rank after the tab was renamed, which is exactly the drift the one-table rename was meant to make impossible, so it reads from that table now. And the masthead's lead figure said 125 builds while the realm shows one armory at a time — it reads 125 MP builds and 8 DMZ builds, because an unqualified total invites a check against a number that is no longer on the page.

🔴 AIRTIME PAINTED THREE BAR STATES AND NAMED NONE OF THEM. Solid is showing, hollow-dashed is scheduled, muted is over — the same shape vocabulary the Track uses, met with no key at all. ⚠️ It is deliberately NOT the shared state key: that one teaches dashed = staged, and a dashed bar here means an announcement that is written and simply has not started yet. Same shape, a neighbouring meaning, and the wrong word would be worse than no word. Like every key in this portal it names only states present on screen, so a week with nothing scheduled does not send somebody hunting for a bar that is not drawn.

🔴 FOUR PANEL SUBTITLES RESTATED THE MASTHEAD THEY SAT UNDER, AND THE MOCKUP'S NEVER DO. Broadcast's was the plainest: 2 live · 1 scheduled · 1 never expires — the masthead's three figures again, sixty pixels below them. Each now says what its own view adds and nothing the figures above it already carry: Broadcast states Discord's per-message embed cap and how many announcements wait for the next message, which is what decides whether a player sees them all at once; the rack states how much of the catalogue is ranked, which is what it sorts by; Access states the grid's dimensions (3 admins × 12 permissions); Health states how much history the tiles are derived from. Found by walking every realm and every tab in one scripted pass and diffing the result against the same walk over the mockup — thirteen pages in two calls.

⚠️ And the rack's Repairs panel was still titled Coverage, with 6 of 8 builds flagged — the pre-rename word, and flagged is the term the masthead split deliberately retired for conflating faults with age. It reads from the same splitCoverage derivation the masthead does now, so the two cannot disagree.

🔴 WHICH IS EXACTLY THE DEFECT THE FIRST VERSION OF THAT FIX INTRODUCED, AND THE NUMBERS CAUGHT IT. It counted aged && !faults — 51 — while the masthead's stale counts every aged build — 106 — so two lines one screen apart used the same word for different numbers. Coverage's own long-standing headline ("66 builds have something actually wrong with them, and 106 more are merely old") always meant the full aged count, so the exclusive reading was both new and wrong. A subtitle written to remove a redundancy is not allowed to create a contradiction, and the only defence is reading it against the figure it sits beneath.

✅ ALERT LEVELS WERE A FILTER AND A PAIR OF TOTALS, NEVER A DISTRIBUTION. errors 24h and quiet alerts 24h sit either side of one line, which answers is anything on fire and not what is this channel actually full of — and an alert level is a decision about who gets interrupted: info is a record, caution is look-when-convenient, error pings a human. The Health panel now draws the seven-day distribution, with pinged counted separately from the level rather than inferred from it, because sendAlert can ping on request and silent alerts are stored but never posted at all. Like every key and legend in this portal it names only levels present in the window — a quiet week must not draw an empty error bar, which reads as a measurement rather than an absence.

🔴 AND THE FIRST VERSION CLONED THE COMPONENT IT SHOULD HAVE REUSED — a duplicate .lvlbars/.lvlb block, 2,400 lines above the original, with the same selectors and different values. The daily-bar charts were then styled by whichever definition the cascade happened to reach last: measured on the page, Alerts per day and Commands per day had swapped to the new geometry. ⚠️ portal:orphans passed the whole time — it asks whether a class has a rule, and both had several. A duplicate selector is invisible to every gate here. The new panel now reuses the component and adds only three level tints, beside the rules they modify.

⚠️ Two more caught by gates the repo already had, both mine. A backtick inside an HTML comment inside a template literal (the build refuses it by name — third time on this branch), and a line ending immediately before an inline <b>, which htm collapses into a run-on word: the same defect fixed in Armory's Coverage sentence earlier the same day, and there is a test for it that named the two lines.

And the Track — the thing the Track tab exists to show — was the SIXTH block on it. Measured at 1280: you clicked Track and the ruler began 863px below the tab, behind the identity strip, a 126px draft card and a 438px staged-changes callout. That callout's own comment says the mockup keeps pending changes "right beside the Track" — the intent was adjacency and the execution was obstruction. It now sits below, where it is still beside it. Ruler at y=1266 → y=761.

Two deadlines on one date were being asserted three separate times, one screen from a panel that modelled them correctly. Battle Pass and Ranked both end Sep 10. The rail drew a chip each, stacked them on two rows over one line with two stems to the same x, and then drew a .dnotch beneath them saying the date was shared — while the season clock in the masthead already read UNTIL SEP 10 · BATTLE PASS · RANKED. Two labels for one moment is a modelling error, so the model changed: group by date before the rows are packed, one chip carrying both names with a key dot each. The notch had nothing left to say and is gone. The test that asserted the old behaviour — "two deadlines on the same day take different rows" — had been passing for exactly as long as the defect existed; it now asserts the merge, with a falsifier proving deadlines on different days still separate.

🔴 --xtop and .dflag.flip were both consumers with no producer, and each had been silently doing nothing since the migration. --xtop is read by .xhair::before and .xd and was set by no code anywhere, so the crosshair's date bubble used its hard-coded 60px fallback forever — the exact defect the mockup records as fixed. .dflag.flip was worse: the rule was scoped .dend .dflag.flip, and .dend is the vertical line on the overlay, not the rail — the same never-matching selector the mockup documents against its own fitFlags(), ported here along with the rule, and no code added the class. Both halves were needed: merging the two Sep 10 chips into one 205px box pushed it 10px past the plot's right edge, where overflow-x:clip ate part of the date. --xtop is now measured rather than summed — the first version added up the scrub, the ruler and the rail, forgot the overview strip, and landed 60px wrong, which is why a fourth copy of three existing measurements is not a fix.

Two draws dated Aug 22 drew two diamonds at one coordinate, and the second one did not exist as far as the page was concerned — no hover, no focus, no tooltip, no way to reach it. clusterPoints was in the mockup, the CSS for it (.ptc.mark.stack, .pt.hid, the same-day ring) was already in the stylesheet, and the JS that would emit any of it was never ported. It branches on the fact, not the pixel condition that triggered it: "2 releases on Aug 22 — the same day, so zooming will not separate them", because the alternative sentence asks for something no zoom can do.

And the pin was never on the rail's layout at all. A pin ("DMZ NOV 11 · 53d beyond this view") welded to the edge in a rail fixed at 52px, so it painted through the Ranked flag. The first fix was wrong in an instructive way: a pin is bottom-anchored where a flag is top-anchored, so giving it a flag's level lifted it toward the flags — measured, worse than the collision. Pins stack among pins; clearing the flags is the rail's job, and railBox() derives the height from the rows actually used. Three duplicate or dead stylesheet blocks went with it: a second .pt.hid, a .ptc.same declared 1,700 lines from its family and painting a second ring over the first, and the retired notch.

⚠️ Every one of these was invisible to the whole gate set. npm test, portal:orphans, portal:coverage and portal:refs were green throughout — they ask whether a class has a rule and whether a function has a test, never whether two elements on one screen agree. What found them was a relational probe: for each pair of rail chips, do their boxes intersect; for each pair of points in a lane, are they within 17px. Both report zero now, from four and one.

The two dead calendar banners are re-hosted, and the fix took a fresh source rather than a script. drawsBannerUrl and eventsBannerUrl were media.discordapp.net links with expired ex= signatures — they rendered as nothing in Discord and nothing in the portal, and no script could repair them because re-hosting needs a source and the sources were gone. Harkirat supplied two fresh signed URLs; both went through utils/calendarBannerCache.js, the mechanism that has been correct since 2026-08-07 and was only ever waiting on an input, and landed at the same two stable public ids. Both databases now point at Cloudinary — prod and the local dev database, the second of which matters because the dev bot and the dev portal read it and would otherwise still render dead links. All three banners can now no longer expire.

And the pending list turned out to be wrong twice in one evening, in the same way both times. Asked what remained, the answer was assembled from the two most recent trackers and missed the two documents that actually hold it: the completion plan's own A–S inventory, and — the one Harkirat meant — the pre-migration design list in a gitignored handoff, which a default rg cannot see. His correction was the same one he had already given once before: "you forgetting ALL the stuff that's still originally pending??" The remedy is structural rather than a resolution to try harder: the new plan names its six sources and instructs that the list be assembled by reading them, never by remembering.

🔴 THE MIGRATION CARRIED THE STYLESHEET AND DROPPED THE MARKUP THAT ACTIVATES IT — and that single sentence explains a class of defect nobody could see. Harkirat: "idk what you were using as reference during the migration but you did not stay true to the mockup design and somehow broke the same things we had already fixed." Literally true, and it has a mechanism. Measured on the running page: the command bar's input renders at 44px inside a 34px wrapper, each painting its own background and its own border — the doubled search bar, fixed weeks ago, back. The fix is still in the stylesheet: :not([data-bare]) opts an input out of the global form reset, and no file in portal/ui/ emits the attribute. Two more of the same shape were found and fixed the same evening — --xtop was read by two rules and set by no code, so the crosshair used its hard-coded fallback forever; .dflag.flip had a rule scoped to the wrong parent and no writer. A rule with no matching element is silent forever, and every gate here asks the opposite question: portal:orphans asks whether a class has a rule, portal:coverage counts emitted classes, npm test renders components and reads their output. A first reverse sweep — does this rule have an *element*? — reported three orphaned data- attributes, three custom properties read but never set, and 48 classes with rules and no emitter, among them Armory's four tier classes and Home's entire card system.

The plan that replaces all of this is one document, and it argues with itself in public. docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-27-portal-conformance.md supersedes the completion plan and folds its A–S inventory in re-verified rather than copied — that inventory had marked the search bar fixed on the same day it was measurably broken. Its falsification pass ran twice, thirty sequentialthinking thoughts, and the second round found that the first draft compared two fixture renderings and called that conformance while the artifact Harkirat actually uses — the real portal, real Mongo, real OAuth — had never been looked at; that it shipped nothing he could look at, despite his acceptance test being visual; and that it had missed five entire bodies of work, including a UX-copy audit that had never been folded into any plan and a login page that appears in none of its parts. Seventeen findings, each recorded with what it would have cost.

⚠️ kind: plan now accepts status: live, and the exception is deliberate. Every plan here had been a frozen snapshot, which is right for a plan written once and then executed and wrong for one that tracks its own execution. Harkirat asked for a plan that "never accidentally goes out of sync." Forcing it to frozen would have made the document lie about its own tense contract — the exact failure the field exists to prevent, pointing the other way. spec deliberately did not gain it: a dated design snapshot is superseded by a new one, never edited.

Light mode was never decided, and now it is. Measured: prefers-color-scheme and data-theme appear zero times in the portal's two stylesheets — it was dark-only by omission, while a tracker row carried "light mode has never been checked at desktop width", a row describing a surface that does not exist and inviting a future session to build one uninvited. It surfaced only because a dimension no inventory listed was checked at all. Harkirat's answer: dark-only is deliberate. The row is retired with its original text kept, per the conservation rule.

🔴 THE GATE THAT ASKED THE OTHER QUESTION — and it found the doubled search bar in its first run. Part 0 of the conformance plan built the inverse of portal:orphans: not does this class have a rule, but does this rule have an element. scripts/portalReverseOrphans.mjs looks for four shapes — a [data-*] selector with no emitter, a var(--x) read with no setter anywhere, a class with two or more rules and no emitter, and a name mismatch, where the class IS emitted and no rule matches it. That last shape is why it parses expressions instead of grepping: armory.js emits its tier rows from a lookup table, so a literal-prefix scanner reports the prefix as an orphan, calls the one working class unemitted, and stays silent about the four rows that really are broken — three wrong answers from one missing capability, and it is a miss that had already happened twice. First run: 4 dead data attributes, 3 unset custom properties, 101 styled-and-unemitted classes, and 6 name mismatches, including the three Armory tier rows emitting t-t3/t-t4/t-t5 against a stylesheet that defines .t-top3/.t-top4/.t-top5. ⚠️ It prints its own blind spot rather than hiding it — 24 class expressions resolve to a variable built elsewhere, so a finding behind one of those may be a false positive, and --why <class> names the emitting file in one command. That is how a class with 74 rules turned out to be emitted after all.

The doubled search bar is fixed, and the fix is one attribute. [data-bare] opts an input out of the global form reset, the reset carries four :not() attribute clauses that put it at specificity 0,4,1, and the .cmdbar input.cb-in rule written to override it sits at 0,2,1 — so the override has been losing the argument silently. Measured before: a 44px input, with its own border, background and radius, inside a 34px bar painting all three. Measured after: 16px, no border, transparent. An opt-out cannot lose an argument it is not having.

And the shell diff found a second defect nobody had reported: the portal was printing its own internal ids at readers. The rail read "season armory broadcast access analytics", the breadcrumb read "season", each realm's panel was titled with its id and the command bar offered "Search season, or run a command" — against a mockup whose rail reads "Season Armory Broadcast", and against COMPANION §2307's explicit rule that the word realm and its ids stay in the code while anything a person reads names the page. One REALM_LABEL map now serves the rail, the crumb, the panel title and the placeholder, because a second copy is how two surfaces come to disagree about what a place is called.

The instruments the mockup shipped with had never been loaded by any page. .grid.js and .peers.js sit beside the eight mockup pages, are copied into the portal's own harness, and not one mockup page included them — so __grid.all() had never once run on the artifact the portal is measured against, and every comparison so far had measured one side with an instrument and the other by eye. A loader in docs/superpowers/mockups/2026-08-23-portal-interactive/assets/shell.js — the one file all eight pages already load, door.html included — gives them ?grid at boot and __instruments() on demand. First reading on Season: 1361 elements examined, 2 near-misses, 33 size issues. The 1282×888 viewport contract is baked into the same instrument: a page cannot resize its own window, so every reading now carries the size it was taken at, and the geometry runner refuses to record an off-contract one.

A third defect, found because a registered state could not reach its own subject: "Copy my Discord ID" acknowledged nothing at all. Both routes to it — the account menu and the command bar — were a bare navigator.clipboard?.writeText(...): no confirmation on success, and in an insecure context or on a refused permission the optional chain swallows the entire action, so a click does nothing and there is no way to tell a silent success from a silent failure. Every other completing action in this portal says so. Both now route through one function that toasts on success and, on refusal, says what to do instead. Five states had been walking vacuously before that — one clicked a role="group" wrapper instead of the toggle inside it, another matched the first [role=menuitem] rather than the one it meant — so each registered state now names the element its own steps are supposed to produce, and a state that does not reach it fails instead of reporting a clean default view under that state's name.

🔴 THE PORTAL RAN AGAINST REAL DATA FOR THE FIRST TIME, AND THREE THINGS THAT HAD NEVER WORKED CAME OUT AT ONCE. Harkirat was away from his machine, so the sign-in went through Discord's QR login — the QR screenshotted out of the live page, scanned from his phone, authorized in chat. /api/review, which the plan records as having "executed in no environment, ever", returned 200 with its ops and changesets on the first request. Everything after that was found in the twenty minutes that followed.

Every banner edit the Season editor has ever staged was born BLOCKED. The identity editor keyed its payload on the field the season document STORES (drawsBannerUrl); calendar.setBanners validates against the page NAMES it accepts (draws, events, playlists). So the op answered Unknown banner page: drawsBannerUrl, the changeset went straight to blocked, and it could never commit. Nothing could have caught it: staging succeeds, and only the Review screen's re-validation ever runs the op against the record again. Two vocabularies for one thing — the same shape as the t-t4/.t-top4 mismatch found the same day, one layer down. A conservation test now reads both lists and fails when they disagree, and it was proven able to fail against the exact key that shipped.

And the screen that would have told you was throwing the sentence away. /api/review read failure.reason — a field no validator sets, because validateSet reports { index, errors: [...] } — so the reader was shown "This change no longer validates" while the system was holding "Unknown banner page: drawsBannerUrl". The portal's own error rule is that a message names WHAT failed, what it MEANS, and ONE action; the generic form gives a reader none of the three.

🔴 A change past character 60 disappeared from the diff entirely. fmtDiffValue truncates a long value for display, and diffRows compared the TRUNCATED strings — so two Cloudinary URLs identical for their first 60 characters and differing only in the tail read as no change at all. A banner edit rendered as an op with zero rows on the one screen in the portal that commits: a change you are asked to approve, shown to you as nothing. It compares the raw values now and formats only for display, and a long value keeps its tail as well as its head, because the end is where a URL, a filename and a version segment actually differ.

Two more instruments, both built to be falsified before being trusted. scripts/portalGeometry.mjs records a realm's grid counts and its inventory — heading, view tabs, column headers, section headings — because __grid reports geometry and not identity: two elements can be perfectly on-grid and be the wrong two. scripts/portalStates.mjs walks a registry of states through the harness and runs three relational passes: a control drawing a second box inside a wrapper drawn tight around it, content clipped to nothing while holding text, and a control no Tab can reach — plus a "modal" the tab order walks out of. 🔴 Relational is the entire point. Every gate this repo had is shaped for each element, assert something about that element, and that shape structurally cannot see two elements disagreeing — which is how a 44px input in a 34px wrapper survived weeks of green suites and two human reports. 13 shell states walk clean, including both door states and the four request failures.

And the geometry fixture failed its own round-trip the first time it was asked to do one. --check immediately after --write, with no code in between, reported Track · nearMisses: 8 → 4 — a smoke alarm going off when nobody is cooking, and the single fastest way to teach a session to re-record instead of to look. Five readings taken inside one settled page were identical, which located it precisely: the reading was stable, the moment it was taken was not. The first view was measured the instant fonts resolved while every later view got a settle after its tab click. Every view gets the same settle now, and a reading is only accepted once it repeats — read, wait, read again, require agreement, and report a surface that never stabilises rather than recording whatever the last attempt happened to see.

⚠️ Three of these instruments were wrong on their first run, and each correction is now a test. The reverse sweep reported all seven .v2-* classes as unstyled because it read two stylesheets where the build concatenates three. The states walk reported nineteen defects in the account menu that were simply a closed panel measuring zero, and then reported a perfectly ordinary field inside a panel as a doubled box — so PASS 1 now requires the wrapper to be drawn tight around the control, since a finding that is wrong three times a run is a finding nobody reads. And the slow-request state failed its own presence check, because the guard asserted on focusable elements and a skeleton legitimately has none. A probe that cannot report presence cannot be trusted to report absence, and each of those is pinned by a case that fails when the fix is removed.

Part 1 — Season, measured against the design surface by surface (2026-08-28)¶

🔴 THAT HEADING OVERSTATES, AND THE CORRECTION IS ADDED IN PLACE RATHER THAN WRITTEN OVER IT — 2026-08-28 16:5x EDT. Every individual claim in the paragraphs below is true and every fix in them holds. Season was not measured surface by surface. Its COMPOSITION was never compared against the mockup at all: the Track sat 530px below the fold behind a context strip the shell did not have, the panel drew a header duplicating the one 60px above it, and TL.days returned NaN on every real record. Harkirat found four such defects in about two seconds by putting two screenshots side by side, immediately after this entry was written.

The mechanism is worth more than the list: every instrument this pass mandated enumerates ELEMENTS, so a page with the right elements in the wrong arrangement passes all of them. The remedy is npm run portal:diff — render both pages and subtract them — and the full account is in the conformance plan's §0.44, §0.45 and §0.46. Season's ledger row was reopened from ☑ to ◐.

The Manifest had never once been recessive, on any realm. COMPANION §10.4's composition rule is four bands — masthead, a context strip that is "a strip, never a panel", the view layer with the strongest treatment, and a Manifest that is "visually recessive… the mechanism beneath the picture" — and the stylesheet implements that last one in a single adjacent-sibling rule. shell.js wrapped each panel in its own <div>, so the two panels were never siblings and the rule had never matched anything. Measured on Season at 1282: the view panel and the Manifest both painting rgb(23,30,36), against the mockup's rgb(23,30,36) and transparent. That is §10.4's own stated failure quoted back at it — "three panels of identical weight where nothing said which mattered" — live on all seven realms. The two ids had no rule and no reader anywhere; deleting them fixed the composition everywhere at once.

A compound selector whose left half is alive is invisible to every gate here. Season's Repairs styled its finding rows as .rephits li while track.js renders .rephits > button — five rules dead, so every finding lost its padding, its hover, and the type contrast between the item's name and the reason it was flagged. The reverse-orphan sweep cannot see this and should not be expected to: .rephits is emitted, so the class is not an orphan; only the descendant was. A sweep that reports classes will never report a dead descendant.

The label-fitting pass on the Track was a two-cycle, and the loop ran through the stylesheet. nolabel sets .bl{display:none}, and a hidden element reports scrollWidth: 0 — so the next pass computed that the label needed 10px, found 68px of clear track, and chose lbl-out, which shows the label again, which restores scrollWidth: 169, which chooses nolabel. Measured live from identical geometry: the same 18px bar read need 10 before a lane collapse and need 179 after it. useMeasured.js's own header describes exactly this loop as the reason the mockup's version could not be ported; the loop was ported anyway, one indirection further back. The label's natural width now comes from a canvas text measurement, which depends on the string and the font and on nothing the pass can set — and whether the label is rendered at all is derived from the plot width rather than measured, so a bar too narrow to hold text does not put 31 characters in a 0×16px box.

lbl-cut was a class name with no rule, in either codebase. The truncate branch had always been a no-op wearing a name — and it works, because .bar .bl is already overflow:hidden with an ellipsis. The branch stays, because the order is the decision (outside, then truncated, then hidden) and a bar wide enough for a clipped label must not fall through to nolabel.

Three ports finished. The mockup's shared-prefix stemming is back — five bars reading "COD Point Rush Week 1".."Week 5" become "Week 1".."Week 5" with the full name on the tooltip and a dotted left edge saying the name was shortened rather than mis-entered. It is computed from the titles, never from rendered width, which is precisely why it was safe to port when its sibling pass was not: nothing it changes feeds back into the decision, and a test asserts it is idempotent on its own output. The Track's zoom hint now renders — .zhint and its kbd had been styled for a line nothing emitted, so the only way to discover the Track's own zoom was to guess it. And the deadline editor's row emits its controls in the order its own grid was written for: both stylesheets say 84px 104px with justify-self:start on the switch, the markup emitted them reversed, and every row stopped 45px short of its own right edge. Nothing was wrong with the CSS.

A Repairs check that reports zero, and means it. COMPANION §5.2's most-cited finding — a calendar banner still pointing at a signed media.discordapp.net link, which 404s once its own deadline passes — is now one of Season's checks. Against the live document it finds nothing, because both databases were re-hosted, and that is the point: a panel that only shows problems cannot tell you what it is watching.

Vocabulary. The manifest's remove column said STAGE DELETION. Delete is the retired word — Remove for reversible, Purge for one-way — and manifest.js already defaulted correctly while Season overrode it.

Three things this pass got wrong about itself, all the same way. An absence read off a state that was never reached: Repairs' zero-state was filed as missing (it is built, and all three checks simply happened to be non-zero in the fixture), the banner rows' rhythm was filed as a footnote defect (it matches the mockup exactly), and eleven "mockup-only" classes turned out to have emitters behind states nobody had opened. The instrument that was right every time was relational — comparing two things that should agree — and both real geometry defects came from a pair disagreeing.

And the mockup's Board was retired three days before the mockup was drawn. season.html and COMPANION §5.2 describe content-state columns; the portal renders the changeset pipeline, which is 2026-08-20-web-admin-portal-design.md §F3. A precedence rule reading "the newer artifact wins" inverts here — the mockup never adopted its own project's decision — and following it mechanically would have rebuilt a screen that had been deliberately replaced. Recorded as COMPANION §16.34, §16.35 and §16.36, because a divergence the design package does not carry is a defect in the package.

Twenty-one Season states are registered and walk clean at 1282×888, and registering them found three more defects: the states driver's type step read a shape none of its siblings use, so it typed nothing into nothing and only the expect guard reported it; a step whose effect mounts the next step's target needed a settle it could not ask for; and the offline banner is reached by ?fail=offline and not by the ?offline= parameter that async.js's own header and this plan's flag list both named — so a state registered under it would have walked the default view and passed.

Finally, the dev portal was serving five-hour-old JavaScript while curl against the same origin returned the new bytes. portal/server.js sent no Cache-Control at all, which is not neutral — a browser then caches heuristically off the file's age. It now sends no-cache, must-revalidate for the document and everything it executes. ⚠️ Cloudflare still overrides that to max-age=14400 on the dev hostname; until a Cache Rule says otherwise, verify a portal change against http://localhost:8787 rather than the tunnel.

2026-08-28 18:5x EDT — the page and the mockup get subtracted, and three of the differences were declarations that never applied¶

Part 1 of the portal conformance pass, second attempt. The first one closed Season on four green gates without anyone opening the page, and Harkirat reopened it with two screenshots. What was missing was not a check but a KIND of check: every instrument in this repo enumerates elements — does this class have a rule, does this rule have an element, do these states walk — and a page with all the right elements in the wrong arrangement passes every one of them. scripts/portalDiff.mjs renders the mockup and the real portal at the same viewport and subtracts them, so the work list is produced before anyone has an opinion about which elements are worth counting.

Three of the differences it found were CSS declarations that had never applied to anything. .mh-add has carried grid-column, grid-row and justify-self:end since the mockup, and Masthead rendered it inside .mh-id — not a grid item, so all three were inert and the ADD row right-aligned to the wrong element: measured on Season at 1282, it ended at x=995 while the export line directly beneath it ended at x=1260. Two right-aligned rows, one above the other, 265px apart. .now::after{content:attr(data-now)} has been in the stylesheet just as long and nothing ever set data-now, so COMPANION's "one thin line and a chip" has never once drawn its chip. And .dfl carried no casing rule, so the same deadline read BATTLE PASS in the masthead and battle pass on the Track's rail, 600px apart on one screen. Armory had the ADD-row defect identically and was fixed by the same change; all seven mastheads were rendered afterwards to prove it, and only Season's geometry fixture moved.

The tool was measuring its own setup. mintSession took AdminUser.findOne({}), which in the dev database is a scoped test admin holding three realms of six — so the rail rendered SEASON / BROADCAST / REVIEW against the mockup's six and three of the first run's eleven regions were the diff reporting its own session. It mints for the hardcoded owner now.

--view refuses rather than attempts, because its failure mode is flattering. Season's Board and Repairs live behind tabs; a click that misses on one side diffs the default view against itself and prints a small, tidy region list that reads like conformance. So each side records what main says before and after the click and the run is refused unless both actually moved — proved both ways, --view Nonsense exits 1 and --view Board lands with the breadcrumb reading Season Board on both sides. Board turned out to need no work at all: COMPANION describes content-state columns, and the portal's changeset pipeline is the supersession recorded in the web-admin-portal design spec §F3.

--viewport exists because the plan's own out-of-scope line could not narrow his instruction. Part 0 named "1280×880 and 375×812"; the execution plan said mobile was out of scope, and that plan was written here, not by him. Both stylesheets carry real max-width:768px rules, so the narrow layout is designed on both sides — 7.3% differ in 12 regions, and what differs is ordering, not degradation.

🔴 One fix was wrong on its first attempt, and the error is worth more than the fix. .srec-nudge inside the season record and .nodraft 60px below it both announced that no next season was staged, so the nudge was deleted as a duplicate. They were not the same fact: the nudge fired only at seven days or fewer, so removing it would have deleted the page's only late warning while looking like tidying. The urgency now rides on .nodraft, which is the line that carries the title field and the button.

Also here: the dev portal stops being cached for four hours at the edge — the zone had no http_request_cache_settings entrypoint at all, so .js and .css through the tunnel took Cloudflare's default over the origin's own no-cache, and a rebuilt portal served a five-hour-old module graph while curl against the same origin returned the new bytes. Verified with a falsifier rather than a green reading: the same zone at a host the rule does not match still returns MISS then EXPIRED at max-age=14400.

Season stays ◐, and the reason is the point of this entry. Five differences remain open with evidence — the Track's Events and Playlists auto-collapsing 20 of 39 items, the overview scrubber's mark weight, Repairs implementing three of COMPANION §5.2's six checks, four export formats against five, and the window range's placement. The difference ledger is local/difference-ledger-season.md (gitignored — state the path). A row that says closed while a difference stands is what produced this second attempt.

2026-08-28 21:1x EDT — the two pages are made to produce the same pixels, and Broadcast reaches 0.3%¶

Harkirat's pivot, and it is the right one: stop adjudicating a 220-row difference list by judgement — which is the component that has been failing — and make the mockup and the wired portal render the same pixels, so closure is a number rather than an opinion. Broadcast, the proving ground: 8.4% across 16 regions and a 274px height gap, down to 0.3% across 28 with the two pages at exactly 1258px.

Three of the four pieces needed less than expected. The data confound did not exist: buildPortal already copies the mockup's fixtures.js into the harness and shasum says byte-identical, so every apparent data difference had been the LIVE SERVER being compared against a fixture. The clock is now frozen on both sides before any page script runs, because ?today= does not travel the countdown and two captures seconds apart could never overlay. ?conform=1 turns off the harness's deliberate demo overrides — its cap of 1 against Discord's real 10 drew one preview card where the design draws two, worth 800 vertical pixels — and publishes data-conform so components read it: Broadcast's mockup has no checkbox column because bulk actions came after the design, and the flag is where that divergence lives rather than a comment nobody can find.

Three of the eleven defects were instruments measuring their own setup. The harness has TWO nested main elements and the height probe took the outer one, so every harness capture was clipped to 888px — the same defect as the morning's, by a different route. The export summary summed NESTED scopes: "6 records" over four announcements, beside a manifest correctly reading "4 of 4"; Season's four scopes are disjoint, which is exactly why it went unseen there. And .mh-take spanning 1/-1 took the strip out of column 2's max-content contribution, so the masthead's two columns sat 80px apart while every individual stat measured identical on both sides — findable only by measuring the columns, never by looking.

The rest were the page, and each one is a class rather than an instance. A padding-left longhand eaten by a padding shorthand later in the same rule (the create button 200px against the design's 202, for this whole pass). A swatch rendered INSIDE the name cell's text span rather than beside it as a flex sibling, which gave every title 17px more room and stopped two of four wrapping where the design wraps them — where a swatch SITS is part of the column's width. Math.round over hours where the design floors from today's midnight, putting every age on the realm one day out. And five pieces of copy, including a note that only ever appeared in its own failure case.

Board is content state again, and the citation that said otherwise was the retired design. docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-20-web-admin-portal-design.md §F3 exists and says exactly what was quoted — it is dated three days before the mockup package that supersedes it, and five before Harkirat wrote that the mockup IS the design. The stylesheet had been agreeing with the newer one the whole time: .bcard.ended, .bmeta.soon and .bcard.staged are rules that mean nothing for a pipeline. The lifecycle port's own first bug was caught by its own new assertion — hasEnded read a point's release date as an end, which is the exact rule the mockup's isEventEnded exists to prevent.

🔴 The method is now the close condition. §0.6 of the conformance plan states it: a realm closes when the rhythm is flat, the overlay reports zero regions above the noise floor on every view at both widths, the inventory's four lists are empty or dated-and-cited, the machine floor is green, a real-server pass has run — and Harkirat has looked. Pixel equality is necessary and NOT sufficient: it cannot see keyboard reachability, copy that is wrong in a way matching the design's own wrong copy, or anything behind an interaction.

2026-08-30 21:55 EDT — every named Season overlay is measured, and the instruments stop contaminating their own readings¶

Season's interaction tier is measured end to end for the first time. All six composer kinds sit at 0.8–1.2%; the expanded identity editor went 10.7% → 0.2% with its 35px height gap closed; the record preview went 18.8% → 0.6%. The three resting views are unchanged at 0.2 / 0.1 / 0.1% throughout, and Broadcast — the shared-surface regression check — holds at 0.3%.

🔴 Every measurement had been changing the next one, and nothing said so.
