The mockup persists five pieces of UI state in sessionStorage — the identity panel, the Board's collapsed columns, the lane-collapse map, the staged-ops tray, the export panel — and portalDiff reused ONE browser page across the mockup shot, the portal shot and the labelling pass. sessionStorage is per-origin and survives navigation inside a tab, so a single --open click on any toggle silently changed what every later run measured, including runs minutes apart. Both instruments now clear it before any page script runs. The recorded figures re-measured identically afterwards — they were sound by luck and are now sound by construction — and one of §L's own open items, "Events and Playlists auto-collapsing 20 of 39 Track items", turns out not to reproduce from a clean slate.

🔴 A stand-down that renders NOTHING is not a stand-down. §0.6a's rule is that a portal-ahead surface renders the mockup's version under ?conform=1. season.js carried conforming() ? null : <DraftZone/>, which removes the surface from the comparison instead — and no styling can close a difference the portal is not drawing. It was 111px of the identity editor's gap. The placement turned out to be the real finding: mounting it unconditionally took the three resting views from 0.2/0.1/0.1% to 13.1/10.2/9.8%, because the design mounts it inside the editor. Seven other conforming() ? null sites are filed for the same question.

🔴 And the absence is half of a conform override. The design's .nodraft box was copied declaration by declaration from its own rule — and every property the portal's base rule sets and the design's does not, display:flex above all, survived. A block paragraph laid out as a flex item and the panel stayed 29px short. The missing properties are computed as a set difference between the two rules and reset explicitly.

The fused accessible name is now a PASS rather than a defect fixed one element at a time. It had been repaired in four unrelated places already; PASS 6 checks it on every realm and every registered state. Its first run found five real elements, four of them outside Season — the shell's commit link announced "4staged · review" on EVERY realm and every state. ⚠️ The detector was wrong twice before its list could be trusted, in opposite directions: looking only at direct children missed a seam two levels down, and counting aria-hidden children invented one that no screen reader hears.

Two instruments learned to refuse rather than guess. --open picked the shortest text match independently on each page, so an ambiguous label had the two sides opening different panels and reporting the difference as conformance — --open "Export first → " compared the design's export drawer against the portal's staging drawer and called it 26.7%. It refuses now. --triggers compared scraped text literally, and the two sides differ in inter-element whitespace by construction, so Board reported four one-sided triggers that were all whitespace. It compares stripped and prints literal. ⚠️ A cross-side panel comparison was tried twice and removed both times — the attempts are recorded because a guard with false positives gets suppressed rather than obeyed.

The real-server pass is a command now, and it cannot measure the door. scripts/portalRealWalk.mjs walks a realm on real Mongo and refuses if it never got past sign-in — the previous hand-rolled attempt reported textLen=784, rows=0 identically on all three views, which reads as a stable measurement and is the signature of never having arrived. Season walks clean: 56 / 45 / 59 rows, zero garbage values.

⚠️ --open-sel <css> exists because two of Season's seven overlays have no unique label — the identity editor opens from a div with no accessible name, and the one-way confirm is one of five buttons reading "Export first →".

2026-08-31 — the portal's two rendering modes collapse into one, and eleven decisions the design got wrong¶

?conform=1 is gone. It had reached 57 conforming() call sites and 52 data-conform blocks — 108 forks where the thing being measured was structurally not the thing that ships, and where a whole class of defect was invisible: a stand-down that rendered nothing where the design renders content cost the identity editor 111px and was found only by opening the overlay. Harkirat's call: treat the ahead rendering as scrapped, keep the conformed one, rebuild redesigns fresh on it. Three surfaces, one code path — mockup, portal on static data, portal on live data.

The measurement settled the ordering, not a preference. 45 of the 57 sites are Season's; Armory, Access, Analytics, Review and Home own none at all, so waiting for all six realms would have bought almost nothing and cost a second pass over the same lines. And the oracle turned out exact by construction: every number in the pass is taken under the flag, so collapsing a site to its flagged value leaves that rendering byte-identical. Broadcast holds at 0.2% with both pages at 1258px, which is the shared-surface check passing.

🔴 A blanket "take the design's version" would have shipped eleven falsehoods. Every conforming() site was read with its surrounding code and the riskiest verified against the stylesheet and the components that consume them: 35 decisions took the design's version, 13 kept the portal's. The four that would have cost most — the day drawer would have lost its entire keyboard path, and the overlay method states in its own coverage note that it cannot see keyboard reachability, so nothing downstream would ever have reported it; oneway.js would have promised an export interlock that does not exist and deleted the typed-confirm field in front of seven irreversible operations; a broken calendar banner would have asserted "image cached and serving" in the branch reached only after its onError had already fired; and the season countdown would have started reading from the start of a fixture day, which is what made two captures comparable and is not a clock for a running console.

So a realm no longer closes on a low percentage. Those 13 keeps are permanent cited differences, so the diff has a floor — Season is +112px on Track and +56px on Board and Repairs, all of it one cascade, attributed by hiding each element and re-measuring rather than by reasoning about it. The close condition is the enumeration: are the regions exactly the cited set. A percentage would let thirteen cited differences hide any number of real ones behind them.

Two gates could not tell a defect from the pass working. .rowlife is emitted with no rule — and the mockup's own season.html emits it on every row and defines no rule for it either, so matching it is correct and removing it would change the class list the audit pairs on. One shared helper now answers "does the design emit this too", and both gates read it; an inherited orphan is reported every run, never fails, and never enters a debt baseline whose own rule is that it only ever shrinks. Both gates were proved still able to fail before their passes were trusted.

Season's audit sections are all worked, and what remains is a floor made of decisions. Triage with the retirement tests encoded: 23 FIX against 83 cited, 40 advisory rule differences the rendered page never shows, 6 sub-pixel, 14 dead in both pages. Five real fixes came out of it, every one the portal having added a declaration the design does not have — the masked ruler tick lacked the design's opacity:0, so a tick's LABEL stayed visible under the NOW chip, which is the one thing masking exists to prevent.

The real-server pass runs clean — past the door, 58/47/61 rows across the three views, one favicon 404. It matters because the harness and the mockup are both fixture-driven: they agree with each other and can both disagree with production.

And portalGeometry never froze its clock, alone among the instruments. The collapse is what made it reproducible: a live countdown changes the width of its readout as digits roll, so a fixture drifted by one between a write and a check seconds later. The tell was two consecutive checks agreeing with each other while both disagreed with the fixture — stable, so not noise; disagreeing, so not the page. A re-record would have buried it.

2026-08-31 15:0x EDT — a compliance hook was rebuilt three times in one afternoon, and each version was falsified by measurement rather than by argument¶

V1 fired on nearly every turn, and hardest on the compliant ones. turn-shape-guard.sh shipped that morning to warn about narration and one-at-a-time work. Its narration test asked whether a text block sat before the first tool call in a message, with $firstTool defaulting to 999 when a message had none — so every text-only message scored as narration. This is a Stop hook, and the last message of a well-formed turn is exactly the one structured summary the working contract demands. It also fired on a plain prose answer, on a turn correctly blocked awaiting push approval, and on the framing before an AskUserQuestion. Three shapes the contract requires. Its suite reported 8/8 throughout.

V2 was mine, and was worse — it matched 0 of 13,922 real messages. Requiring the prose to sit before a tool call in the same message describes a shape this transcript format cannot produce: text and tool calls are always separate assistant messages. A 140-character floor was added on the theory that real narration is long. The suite went 21/21 on synthetic fixtures while the rule was dead.

Then the length theory was inverted, and then falsified outright. The first correction was that narration is short — "Found it." is nine characters, and the measured histogram peaks at 50–100 while the floor sat at 140. Harkirat falsified that too, with a screenshot of a real session: page-long structured blocks, tables included, sitting between tool calls all morning. Measured across 3,775 real instances: 13 to 7,869 characters, median 128, mass in every band. 🔴 Length is not the discriminator in either direction. Position is — a text-only message with more tool calls after it is mid-turn commentary, whatever it says and however long. The rule is now purely positional, with no regex, no length bound and no tunable constant, and only the two carve-outs Harkirat states himself: a note while waiting on a long background task, and the framing immediately before a popup.

🔴 And one binary trigger was still wrong, because narration is situation-dependent. Position detects a candidate; it cannot judge one. A single substantive checkpoint halfway through a long autonomous run is legitimate — the same block repeated after every tool call is running commentary, and the earlier versions treated them identically, which is what made the hook read as friction rather than help. Each mid-turn block is now classified on four independent signals: HEDGE (opens by pre-registering intent — delete it, there is nothing to move), ACK (a contentless reaction), DUPLICATE (its distinctive words already appear in the turn's own final summary, so the reader pays twice), and CADENCE (prose keeping pace 1:1 with the work). A block that is none of these stays silent.

🔴 The test underneath all four is redundancy and importance, and only the session can apply it — Harkirat's framing: is this important enough to say right now, or can it wait for the checkpoint summary, and will it be repeated there anyway? DUPLICATE approximates that mechanically by word overlap with the final message; the warning also asks the question outright, because a guard that reports only a count teaches silence, and the goal is compliance.

🔴 The deeper error was optimising for RARITY when the target is TRUTH. Every threshold was being tuned to make the hook fire less: at run ≥3 it fired on 71.5% of 615 real turns, at ≥8 on 51.4%, at ≥20 on 30.1% — no cut point existed, and moving 2→3 changed 76.6% to 71.5%, which is nothing. "A good alert is a rare alert" comes from monitoring, where alerts compete for a human's scarce attention. The reader here is Claude, so alert fatigue is not the governing constraint and the rate IS the finding: narration occurs in 76.6% of turns at a mean of 6.1 per turn against a contract of zero.

And the clauses were split across three events, because a Stop hook is a post-mortem that cannot change the turn it measures. Asking which event each clause wants is the question the first two versions never asked. batch-edit-guard.sh is PreToolUse: it fires at the second edit to a file already edited this turn, while the rest can still be collapsed into one heredoc, and it has no escape hatch — unlike a read-chain, a second edit to a known file is never waiting on the first one's output, and any non-edit call resets the map by construction so edit → test → fix-what-the-test-found does not fire. audit-think-gate.sh is UserPromptSubmit, covering the one contract clause carrying the word mandatorily: sequential thinking on an audit or review. turn-shape-guard.sh keeps only what is genuinely retrospective.

⚠️ The suites gained the case class whose absence let two broken versions ship: a replay against real transcripts, asserting the rule fires on some turns and is silent on others. A predicate that hits 0% or 100% of real turns is broken whatever the hand-written cases say — and neither V1 nor V2 could have failed a hand-written case. On the shipped version the replay reports 38 of 40 real turns firing, which is not a tuning failure but the measurement of how much narration these sessions actually contain.

2026-08-24 — the last three mockup surfaces are rebuilt on the bot's real schemas, and the rule meant to prevent exactly this failed¶

Season, Broadcast and Access were rebuilt onto the bot's real Mongoose schemas instead of hand-authored fixtures, and doing it surfaced defects in shipped code, in the mockup, and in the rule written to stop this happening. Three of the five commits touch shipped code.

Season. A draw has ONE date and no end at all — only a calendar row carries date + endDate. So three of six lanes hold points, not bands, and the Track had been drawing a duration the schema does not have. A draw with no explicit calendar row is served synthetic and dateOnly, and isEventEnded() returns false for it forever — 11 of 14 real draws are in that state. Tiers are lowercase words plus comment, which is not a tier at all but a subtext note.

Broadcast. models/Announcement.js has six fields and the mockup had invented four. title+body — there is one text, and the header had been removed on 2026-08-13 at Harkirat's own correction, so the split silently re-introduced what he had deleted. pinned — no such field. **A drag-to-reorder priority: the page's primary interaction was a field that exists on no model. And views: 12840 — fabricated telemetry, the worst kind of fixture error because it is indistinguishable from data.** Reach now comes only from UserPreference.seenAnnouncementIds and renders only when non-zero, which for all four announcements is never.

Access. The editor role was fictional, not merely unenforced — and the deferred-list entry describing it as "visible but unenforced" was an active invitation to go and build it. Eleven permission tokens, not seven. Grants and revokes are direct writes rather than ops, with typed-Discord-ID confirmation and no staging leg.

🔴 AND THE RULE THAT FAILED IS THE REAL ENTRY HERE. COMPANION §3.9 told a session to read four sources before designing: the model, the action registry, the parser, the renderer. All four are bot-side. Following it exactly still left portal/api/*.js and portal/ui/*.js unread — and those were already built and AHEAD of the mockup on two realms. portal/ui/access.js already had the permission grid with direct-vs-inherited, single-points-of-failure and typed-ID confirmation while access.html still showed a fictional role and 7 of 11 tokens.

A stale mockup is worse than a wrong fixture. A wrong fixture produces a wrong render and somebody notices. A stale mockup is the instruction — the package is the design source of truth — so wiring it faithfully would have been a deliberate rollback of working design, executed carefully, by someone doing exactly what they were told. §3.9 now names five sources.

2026-08-28 — Cloudflare served four-hour-stale JS over the origin's own no-cache¶

Recorded here because it cost real debugging time and the archive entry is easy to miss: the dev portal's JavaScript was cached by Cloudflare for four hours over the origin's own no-cache header, so a fix that had shipped kept reading as unfixed. The full account is in docs/archive/resolved-list.md. ⚠️ The general shape is the one this branch kept meeting from a different direction — a verification that is measuring something other than what you think it is measuring — and it is why the asset cache-buster became an enforced gate two days earlier rather than a hand-bumped stamp.

2026-08-25 — eleven checks existed and CI ran none of them, and the last hand-bumped step became a gate¶

portal:gate, portal:refs and portal:roundtrip were absent from npm test's chain, and CI runs npm test. So the schema check, the parse and undeclared-identifier checks, a backtick lint added that morning, the cache-buster check added that morning, two COMPANION checks added an hour earlier, and the export round-trip against the real adminParser.js ran only when somebody typed them by hand — eleven checks, over two days.

🔴 .github/workflows/ci.yml already carried a comment about this exact failure from 2026-08-02: "The tests were fine. Nothing was running them. A test nobody runs is worse than no test, because it produces a documented belief that the behaviour is covered." It happened again anyway, which is the argument for the fix being verified rather than asserted: the three gates were put in the chain and then proven by planting a wrong permission-token count in COMPANION.md and watching npm test go red, then restoring it and watching it go green — not by reading package.json.

The cache-buster was the last admitted-unenforced step. COMPANION §15.8 said so in as many words — the ?v= stamp is "bumped by hand when an asset changes" — while a stale asset had already produced three false "verified" claims in that package's history and thirty-five references had just been bumped by hand with nothing checking. The invariant needs no judgement: no asset may be newer than the ?v= stamp of the pages referencing it. ⚠️ It uses mtime, so a fresh clone can report a false positive — the safe direction, since the remedy is to bump and bumping is free. ⚠️ The two browser harnesses still cannot run in CI; that is a limitation, not an oversight, and it is now stated wherever the "ALL CLEAN — 73 passes" figure is quoted, because that number comes from a human running it.

2026-08-31 16:1x EDT — a gate at the decision point was built, measured and deleted, and a merge whose "no conflicts" claim had expired¶

A PreToolUse gate on AskUserQuestion was built and then deleted the same hour. Twice in one session an already-settled decision went into a popup — most visibly whether Armory's overlays were in scope, while the conformance plan's realm table already read "Armory … earns the full overlay treatment incl. the interaction tier" — with the query-the-ledger-first rule loaded from three separate files. Prose had demonstrably failed, so the shape that works here was tried: a check at the single act.

🔴 It failed its falsifier in both directions at once. On the real failing question it surfaced five near-misses and missed the line that answers it, because the question said "overlays" and the table says "overlay". On a control question about a weapon rarity badge gradient — nothing to do with the portal — it fired five hits anyway. That second result is the structural one: the corpus is the decision ledger plus the deferred list plus CLAUDE.md plus every plan, which together mention every topic in the project, so any project question matches something. Rarity weighting fixes the ranking, not the base rate. A lexical gate over a corpus that mentions everything cannot be precise, and an imprecise gate at a decision point is pure friction. Filed under Decided-no with the measurement, because the motivation will recur.

And the sibling merge's headline claim had expired. Its handoff said zero file overlap, true when written on 2026-08-30 23:47 and false by the time it was merged, because this branch edited docs/db-deferred-list.md twice that day. Neither the default nor the histogram diff algorithm could align it — both sides had inserted large blocks — and git apply --3way cannot run against a conflicted index, which has no stage 0. Resolved by computing base→theirs opcodes and placing each of the six hunks after the last preceding context line that is unique in the target, so the insert point is located rather than guessed, then verifying conservation in both directions: all 8 lines theirs added present, all 474 lines ours added present. Verifying the claim rather than trusting it is the only reason the conflict surfaced before the merge instead of after.

Pre-Release v3.68.0

#175

The old /draw calculator was a setup form: pick a draw, pick a goal, open a modal, type two numbers, submit, press Calculate — five interactions before a single figure appeared, and Harkirat called it "terrible, lacks intuitive, lacks design/style, and is not user friendly." It is rebuilt from the ground up.

One always-live panel, not two stages. Every figure is a pure function of the state carried in the button/select customId, so recomputing on every click costs a few thousand integer operations against a Discord round trip — there was never a reason for a separate "Calculate" step. pullsDone and the target pull are now selects, enumerated from the draw's real pull count, so an out-of-range value can no longer be typed in the first place; only genuinely free-form amounts (a CP balance, a CP budget) still open a one-field modal. A real landing state was added — the command used to open straight into a random draw with no explanation of what the dropdowns or buttons were for.

Rebuilt a second time against Harkirat's own mockup. Three earlier passes each guessed at "better structure" from first principles and were each rejected on his live screenshots. He then exported a real Components V2 message he'd built himself, and the COST BREAKDOWN block was rebuilt to match it directly — reusing /draw prices' own buildDrawEntries() for the top summary so the two commands render the same draw identically instead of two similar-but-different copies, and adding progressive disclosure ("Show Breakdown" / "Simplify") so the collapsed view isn't a wall of numbers.

Three rounds of live mobile polish followed, each from a screenshot on the running dev bot: code-spans are now reserved for the figures a player actually acts on (total price, total CP, what's left over) rather than boxing every number, since a long or multi-part value wraps mid-box on a narrow phone; the blockquote-prefixed label marker was replaced with a plain bullet after it rendered as an unwanted vertical bar down the page; and the region label moved off the ## COST BREAKDOWN heading onto its own caption line after it started wrapping into the title.

The two commands are cross-linked (/draw calculator ↔ /draw prices, zero new handler code either way, both routing through each command's own existing custom_id scheme), and three new emoji assets were added (calculator, mythicCard, mythicCoin) — verified against the dev application only, since prod credentials aren't available from this worktree.

Not yet click-tested live end-to-end on the dev bot in a formal pass (it was exercised heavily via the live screenshot-feedback loop above); filed in docs/db-deferred-list.md's 🔔 Reminders with the specific sequence still owed.

The check now runs before any mutation, and the test asserts the rejection is clean rather than merely loud.

Pre-Release v3.65.0

#173

The plan and spec filed in v3.64.0, built — and then substantially rebuilt, five times, against a real Discord client on desktop and on a phone. The rebuild is the bigger half of this release and most of it came from looking at the rendered thing rather than re-reading the design.

The five pages. Discord is a glance now; the portal carries the depth. 🔴 Timing was asserting a production fault that did not exist. It measured total duration against Discord's 3,000 ms limit — but that limit is the deadline to acknowledge an interaction; after a defer the window is fifteen minutes. A heavy image command working exactly as designed rendered as 🔴 /colors -204% headroom. Headroom now applies to the ack alone; duration gets a felt-speed band on Nielsen's published thresholds.

🔴 And nobody could read it anyway. p50, p95 and "headroom" all failed on the page's only reader. They are "usually", "slowest 1 in 20", and the rule plus what it consumes — translations chosen to stay true, not merely simpler.

🔴 Revert used to fire blind. A row read "Added new draw" and offered a button that immediately undid it. Tapping now opens a detail panel that renders the actual record, using the record's own renderer — a draw draws itself exactly as /draws shows it — with a real before/after for edits, reconstructed from the inverse's stored previous values. Revert lives in there behind a red button, beside an Edit that dispatches through the existing action registry. Crucially it also names any later change that touched the same record, because reverting writes old values back over whatever came after it.

Mobile changed several verdicts. ANSI colour is stripped silently on iOS, so colour is decoration and never meaning — severity leads with a glyph instead. The VM-peaks block ran 46 columns and wrapped into four ragged lines; the real budget measures near 32, not the 40 the spec estimated, and that spec had cited the wrapping function itself as its own precedent.

And docs-audit's superseded_by existence check had never once executed, because nothing in the repo used the field; it threw a ReferenceError on first use while its own self-test passed the entire time, because a crashed check reports under the same id as a real finding. Both the check and the self-test harness are fixed — a proof is now rejected if the check only "reported" by crashing.

Change ids are #284 now rather than Aug22-28, which read as a second, contradicting date beside the real timestamp. Old ids still resolve.

Pre-Release v3.64.0

#172

Four items off the deferred list, one deferred by name, and one turned into a spec instead of code.

Every failed /manage submit now hands you your work back. A rejected add, edit, or bulk paste replies with what you entered — reconstructed in that entity's own bulk format, so it pastes back into either the field it came from or that entity's Bulk Add — plus a Try Again button that reopens the same form already refilled. 14 modals, 12 failure branches across draws, calendar and loadouts. The button rather than a modal is Discord's rule, not a preference: a modal submit cannot be answered with another modal. The snippet and the button expire differently on purpose — the button lasts 10 minutes, the text doesn't expire at all — which is why both were worth having.

Loadout images can be a URL now. The Cloudinary Image Key field on Add and Edit takes either a Public ID or a pasted image link, told apart by the URL scheme, so it needed no sixth field in a modal that was already at Discord's hard five-field cap. On Edit the upload lands on the build's existing key, so swapping a picture never breaks anything pointing at it. If Cloudinary is unreachable the raw URL is saved instead of the save failing — already a supported state, and the same fallback draw thumbnails have always had.

The loadout bulk format was rewritten, and the complaint behind it turned out to be exactly right. Asked why some things were on one line and others on their own, the honest answer was that there was no principle to state. There is one now — identity on the first line, every optional field on its own labelled line, everything else an attachment — and the old seven-segment pipe line is rejected outright rather than half-parsed, at Harkirat's call.

Mode is gone from the format; the page has always been what decided it.

/bot analytics got a design spec and an 8-task plan rather than a rebuild. What is real is that all five pages are one skeleton differing only in accent colour, so on a quiet bot they collapse into the same near-empty panel. Mid-drafting the whole thing was reframed: the web portal now carries in-depth analytics, so Discord becomes a glance — one question, one screenful, with pagers and filters and exports moving to the portal. Both the detection and, for Replace specifically, a flag-CHANGE warning (an existing event's flag silently flipping on an unrelated re-paste) are now surfaced directly in the confirmation message, not left to be discovered once already live.

Pre-Release v3.59.0

#168

Plan 2 of the portal operation-core refactor: calendar/loadouts/patchnotes/season/announcements now all route their DB mutations through core/changeset.js's commitSet, matching the pattern plan 1 already established for draws — every mutation validates as a batch, applies inside one real Mongo transaction, and records a ChangeLog row carrying a real inverse. The old in-memory Undo store (handlers/manage/shared.js's registerUndo/manageUndoStore) is retired entirely; every entity's revert now lives permanently on /bot analytics' Changes page (core/revert.js), backed by Mongo instead of a same-session-only Map that vanished on restart.

A 13-agent code review across the whole branch (both plan 1 and plan 2's ranges) found 10 real bugs, all fixed. The two most severe were both in the operation core itself, not in any one entity: commitSet validated its ops array before flattening it, so any op whose invert() returns an ARRAY (draw.bulkDelete/draw.purge, and the newly-added loadout.bulkAdd/bulkReplace) made clicking Revert fail unconditionally with "unknown op type undefined" — the exact shape core/revert.js's revertChange always produces; and pageForOp always took action[0] of a multi-page-registered op, permanently mislabeling every DMZ loadout mutation's ChangeLog row as loadouts_mp, which would have both broken analytics' page filter for DMZ and let a loadouts_mp-scoped admin revert a DMZ change they hold no grant for (or blocked a loadouts_dmz-scoped admin from reverting their own). Also fixed: draw.bulkAdd computed its new ids via a post-resort tail-slice, which silently grabs the wrong ids — and therefore deletes the wrong draws on revert — whenever a newly-added draw's date sorts earlier than an existing one; loadout.bulkAdd/bulkReplace's invert() only deleted newly-created docs, leaving any build the same paste overwrote in place permanently un-revertable; a transaction-retry accumulator bug where changeIds/results could double-count across a MongoDB TransientTransactionError retry; editLoadout hanging an interaction forever on a stale id (deferred, never followed up); two unawaited replies in handlers/bot.js's revert branch, against the documented crash-net convention; previewSet crashing on any bulk op; a read-side gap where the already-settable Announcement.startsAt was never checked; and a bare docs:audit npm script silently dropped by an earlier merge-conflict resolution, breaking CI's audit step for 9+ commits without anyone noticing.

7 lower-severity findings from the same review were fixed in a follow-up pass, not left deferred: core/mongo/positional.js gained a shared resortByDate (hoisted out of a byte-identical draws.js/calendar.js duplicate, now returning the sorted array so both entities' bulkAdd drop a redundant third fetch); core/ops/patchnotes.js's Cloudinary uploads now run via Promise.all (verified safe against the transaction session first); handlers/manage/patchnotes.js's reloadEntry() post-commit-read bandaid is gone, replaced by title/imageCount surfaced directly on the op's own applied, matching how the other 4 entities solved the same problem; a handful of dead exports and duplicated logic were cleaned up, including a shared extractCommitError(result) helper replacing 31 copies of the same error-extraction expression across the 6 entity handlers.

Full npm test green throughout; npm run check/docs:audit/docs:reflow/docs:reflow-comments all clean.

Pre-Release v3.58.0

#167 ccca561

Ported speed wins from the gif-background-remover skill's own harness work: node --check runs -P 8 (44.6s → 1.7–5.0s); .claude/hooks/run-all-tests.sh replaces a hand-rolled busy-poll scheduler with xargs -P (53.4s → 16–21s); scripts/docs-audit.test.mjs's 71 checks are now sharded across N node subprocesses (~110–115s → ~40–55s), guarded by a cross-shard total-slot-count invariant so a desynced or malformed shard assignment fails loudly instead of reporting a false pass.

New scripts/testCache.mjs is a session-scoped cache (gitignored local/.test-cache/): hashes actual input bytes plus the wrapped command, skips re-running only on an exact match to a prior pass, never caches a failure, and treats CI=true as an automatic bypass so CI's own deliberate second docs:audit:test invocation still re-runs for real rather than replaying a cache hit within the same job. Wraps docs:audit:test and test:hooks; full npm test drops from ~92s cold to ~28–31s warm.

Two full rounds of parallel code review (8 finder angles each), all findings fixed, caught real defects — not cosmetic ones. Round 1 (10 findings): HOOK_TEST_JOBS=0 deadlocked the hook suite forever; the cache's own self-test leaked real cache files into the repo (local/.test-cache/ isolation was broken by a cwd override that had no effect on where testCache.mjs actually resolves its cache directory, since that's derived from the script's own file location); a cache entry was keyed on input-file hash alone, never the wrapped command, so changing package.json's command without touching the hashed files would have served a stale pass for code that was never executed; a spawn failure was silently downgraded to a bare exit code with no diagnostic text. Round 2 (7 findings, on the docs-audit sharding specifically): the single most severe defect this branch produced — a malformed DOCS_AUDIT_TEST_SHARD value made every check silently skip while docs-audit.test.mjs still printed ✅ all 0 checks proven capable of failing, a self-congratulating false pass in the file whose entire job is catching exactly that failure mode. Fixed with a parse-time validation that refuses to run rather than silently skip, plus a cross-shard invariant (every shard must agree on the total check-slot count, and executed checks summed across shards must equal it) that structurally can't be bypassed the way the unguarded version was.

A third bug, caught by direct verification rather than either review round: the fix for the total-slot-count invariant itself had a || short-circuit (SHARD_N <= 1 || __idx++ % SHARD_N === SHARD_I) that skipped the counter increment entirely on the default unsharded path — which would have produced a false-positive "some checks silently never ran" failure the first time anyone ran DOCS_AUDIT_TEST_JOBS=1. Found by actually running that exact configuration and reading the number, not by reasoning about the code. Fixed and re-verified under that configuration, plus a real failure-injection re-check (a deliberately broken check correctly caught, exactly one failure reported, byte-identical file restoration afterward) on the final code.

Pre-Release v3.56.0

#165

Nothing changed in the bot. v3.55.0 shipped citing a literal (#PR); this fills it to (#164), backfills v3.54.0's squash hash 9cb560a, and adds a changelog-pr-cite ERROR check to scripts/docs-audit.mjs so the class cannot recur. The placeholder is structural rather than careless, which is why a check rather than more care: the pre-merge changelog entry is composed on the branch, where the PR number does not yet exist. Every audit check passed on it — version coverage, hash chain, record structure — because none of them read whether a citation is a number. The check is deliberately narrow, flagging placeholder shapes only ((#PR), (#XXX), (#TBD)) and never a missing citation, which has legitimate historical instances in that file. It scans headings only, so a body paragraph discussing the placeholder does not trip it — verified by appending one and confirming the audit stayed green.

The check failed twice before it worked, and both failures were silent. It first returned a problems key: every other check in that file returns findings, the runner reads only that, so it passed green while doing nothing — vacuous in exactly the case it existed for. It then returned bare strings, which the renderer prints as undefined while still failing the run. Neither was visible from reading it; both were caught by injecting (#PR) and watching the exit code. Both causes are now comments at the return site, and a proves() case pins the behaviour. The structural remedy is ordering, not diligence — open the PR first, then write the entry with the real number — and that is what this release did.

Pre-Release v3.55.0

#164

Nothing changed in the bot. A design-only pass producing docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-20-web-admin-portal-design.md and three dependency-ordered plans for portal.dioreo.app — a browser admin console, Discord-OAuth-gated, that does everything /manage does plus scheduling, previewing, diffing and search-then-tick bulk editing that a Discord modal physically cannot host. /manage stays live and its behaviour unchanged. Ships after v3.0.0. This supersedes the [P2 · L] "real search + multi-select flow" roadmap item — Harkirat changed his mind on the implementation, not the goal, so that item is struck in place in both trackers rather than deleted, and .claude/rules/manage-panel.md's own "Build the real version next, not a silent gap" instruction was struck too: that file auto-loads on any commands/manage.js edit and would otherwise have read as a live to-do.

The design is an operation algebra — every mutation becomes a value { type, target, payload } with four verbs (validate/preview/apply/invert) that both Discord and the web drive, which also gives /manage durable undo surviving a restart, replacing an in-memory closure Map. A three-tier hybrid model derived from reversibility rather than assigned per button, where tier 3 will not commit until what it destroys has been exported — nearly free, because utils/adminParser.js's formatters already round-trip through its own parsers. Element-identity concurrency, forced by reading the schema: SeasonalData is one global document, so ordinary __v locking would fire false conflicts on every pair of unrelated edits while a plain .save() silently reverts the other one. And a two-layer information architecture across five realms, with shape carrying state and colour carrying topic — Harkirat's correction, and the better rule, because shape survives greyscale and colourblindness.

All six premises the design rests on were measured rather than assumed, and one nearly derailed it for a reason unrelated to the design: transactions work on the M0 cluster (probed in a throwaway database, 0 of 2 after a rollback, 2 of 2 after a commit), element-identity concurrency behaves exactly as specified including rejecting a stale prior-value assertion, storage is at 0.15% of 512 MB, the VM has 390 MB available with the bot at 131 MB — not the ~600 MB the spec had derived from month-old figures — buildLoadoutCard() imports zero discord.js and yields production emoji ids without a client, and cloudflared is not installed. The near-miss: the transaction probe was pinned to .env.dev by a guard written to keep it safe, and that database is a standalone, so it would have failed and been read as "M0 does not support transactions".

A reader-test agent with no session context found 28 defects that three falsification passes had missed, and every one spot-checked was confirmed. Four were fatal — a circular require that made the first file fail on load with a TypeError, a conservation test mathematically incapable of passing over a 1:1 map holding ten actions and seven ops, three of seven inverses destroyed by re-validation so undo silently restored nothing, and recordChange returning undefined with no session so audit rows escaped the transaction. One was a privilege escalation: the Revert control trusted the bot_ router prefix, which proves some /bot access rather than page scope. Three were false claims about existing code, each a single grep away — patchConsole() takes no parameters, scripts/buildLegalPages.js has no module.exports, handlers/router.js never imports ALLOWED_ADMIN_ID. The generalizable lesson is recorded in the spec's audit log: the earlier passes audited the design and never ran the plan's own code as code.

Repairing those exposed a second bug, in this repo's own tooling. An orphaned fence left by one of the fixes gave a plan an odd fence count; scripts/reflow-prose.mjs pairs fences positionally, so a later opening fence was consumed as an earlier block's close and nine code blocks after that point were reflowed as prose and collapsed onto single lines, including an entire module implementation. verify() passed, because it compares fenced-block content and under a mispairing compared the same wrong blocks before and after — a vacuous check. The plan was restored from the last clean commit and all 22 fixes re-applied deterministically; reflow-prose.mjs now reports an odd fence count as its own problem before any content comparison, with two test cases including a falsifier for the guard itself, proven by disabling it and watching the suite go red.

Pre-Release v3.53.0

#162 a5f626b

Ships the design from docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-20-hotpatch-design.md. utils/hotpatch.js computes a static require-graph closure for a set of changed files and classifies it ALLOW / REFUSE_STATE (live module state with no __hotSwap contract) / REFUSE_STRUCTURAL (index.js/bot//models/ in the closure, or an unresolved path) — the invariant is that a reload is sound iff its closure terminates at a late-bound boundary and every member is stateless or opts in. handlers/router.js now resolves its 15 handler modules at call time instead of capturing them once at require, which is what makes them hot-swappable and what keeps router.js itself a boundary rather than a closure member. applyHotpatch is verify-then-swap, all-or-nothing: a node --check syntax gate, a snapshot of require.cache and client.commands, the actual swap, shape validation (a changed Discord-facing command shape — new command, changed option or description — is refused, since the command list only updates via one REST PUT at boot), then either re-wire or roll back to the exact snapshot. Two fire surfaces: /bot hotpatch (owner-only, pull/dry_run/file options, a panel that either confirms what applied or refuses with a reason plus Full-restart/Cancel buttons) and scripts/hotpatch.mjs over a SIGUSR2 signal to the running process, for the phone/no-Discord case. The baseline commit a hotpatch diffs against comes from utils/logger.js's currentCommit() (now a getter over a hotpatch-updated let, via the new noteHotpatch()), never git rev-parse HEAD — Harkirat pulls separately and then hotpatches, so HEAD is already the new commit by the time a hotpatch runs, and diffing against it would silently no-op forever. Ships with zero __hotSwap declarations by design; nine files hold nearly all the blockable state and each opts in only when it actually blocks a wanted patch — see .claude/rules/hotpatch.md. Also fixes .claude/hooks/self-check.sh's model-selection gate, found live during this branch's own completeness sweep: the gate's "already given, do not repeat it" short-circuit checked only the model-derivation shape, so stating that alone silently satisfied its own request for the /rename string too. Adds a second, deliberately stricter detector for the rename-string shape and requires both before going quiet.

Pre-Release v3.51.0

#159 07b67e2

The website's fourth page family: /commands, a reference for every public Dioreo command that reads the bot's own command builders at build time, so it cannot drift from what the bot actually registers. scripts/lib/commandCatalog.js calls .toJSON() on every module in commands/ and files each leaf under the group commands/help.js's own CATEGORY_DEFS puts it in — so the website and the in-Discord directory cannot disagree about how the bot is organised — and throws, naming the command, if a public one has nowhere to go. scripts/lib/commandProse.js supplies the one thing Discord cannot: why a person would want the command, gated both ways so prose without a command and a command without prose both fail the build. scripts/lib/commandsPage.js renders it. Accent is Signal Green 121°, the midpoint of the widest gap on the nav's hue wheel (citron 62° → teal 180°), and the nav restaged from six tabs to seven, ten inside /changelog/, both tiers measured in a browser rather than arithmetic'd from the old ones.

The misalignment Harkirat reported was not a design problem, and the cause is worth writing down. .bar, .bar nav{margin-left:auto} and .page — the site's entire chrome layout — were written out verbatim in shell(), warmShell() and scripts/lib/chronicle.js: three byte-identical copies and no shared constant. So a fourth family could be added carrying the bar markup and none of its styling, and every gate stayed green, because the build checks content, links, class collisions, contrast and coverage and never whether a class resolves to a rule at all. Measured on the shipped file: public/commands.html contained zero .bar, .bar nav, .page or #prog rules. Extracted as CHROME.BAR_CSS and CHROME.PAGE_CSS and collapsed all three copies; the other eight pages are unchanged apart from one emitted CSS comment that is now a JS comment (terms.html is 768 bytes lighter, contributing.html and changelog/index.html identical ignoring whitespace). The three markup deviations went with it: the bar's four controls now sit inside the <nav> that margin-left:auto targets, the content sits in .page instead of a private wrapper 40px narrower with no top padding for the fixed bar, and pageFoot() is the last child of .page rather than stretching to the full viewport.

A phone could not reach the command list at all. .cx-fold{display:none} sat after the media rule that shows it; both selectors are (0,1,0), so source order decided and the base rule won at every width — the button was never visible anywhere. Combined with setOpen() deliberately collapsing the picker below 880px, a phone got a search box, no list, and no control to open one, on the page most likely to be read on a phone. Fixed by moving the base declaration above the media block and verified at a real 390px touch viewport: the button measures 39px, one click opens 340px of list and all 16 rows. Two coarse-pointer targets that measured 27px and 31px were raised past 32px in the same pass.

The page is "the Receiver", and it took five rounds to get there. The one before it — two zones, a dot column, a coloured panel — was chosen from renders and then failed on a phone, which is where this page is read. Measured at 375×812: the command index began 2.3 screenfuls down and was 855px tall, one command's panel was 1282px, and the command line — the artifact a reader came for — sat at y=1339, below everything. A layout whose whole premise is "both zones always on screen" had a mobile mode where neither was, and it degraded into exactly the single-scrolling-column shape that had already been rejected two rounds earlier. The page now has one shape in both modes: a rail of fourteen coloured command chips that wraps into grouped rows on a wide screen and scrolls horizontally on a narrow one, and a panel whose command line is sticky — under the rail on desktop, pinned to the bottom of the viewport on a phone. Opening a command on mobile fell from a 3010px document to 1219px, and the panel itself from 1282px to 660px, because a fifteen-item timezone list is now a 46px row you open rather than 348px you scroll past. The interaction is still :target, so it still needs no JavaScript, and there is now a way back — the rail's first chip and the Escape key. There was none: the only route to the landing state was the "Who sees it" link, which pointed at a guide inside the home panel, so following it silently discarded the command you were reading.

The panel stopped describing the command and started building it. Options were read-only pills and the one required option — the one that decides whether the command runs at all — was a bordered read-only block wearing a REQUIRED badge, which every convention on the web reads as disabled. The affordance was exactly inverted: the only control that mattered was the only one you could not touch. A required option is now a real control — a text input seeded with the sample when Discord takes free text, a pre-selected pill set when it takes a fixed list, and never both wrong ways round. And a required option can no longer fall out of the copy line. The client repaint built the line from the set of values the reader had picked; a free-text required option can never be in that set, so /timestamp datetime sun 4:30pm became /timestamp timezone (UTC−04:00) Eastern the instant anything optional was touched, and the page handed the reader a command Discord rejects. The line is now built from the command's option list, every option holds a permanent seat, an unfilled one draws as a visible gap, and Copy refuses with "Needs datetime" rather than copying something broken.

An identity colour was being used as a text colour, and that was the worst thing on the page. Each command's accent is picked for a Discord embed, and the page was bending it into readable text by walking its lightness until it measured 4.5:1. Patch Gold #F2C230 came out #7C5F08 in light theme — a 31-point lightness drop, which is brown — Neon Amber came out rust, and the raw hex sat in a dot forty pixels away, so the page showed two different colours for one command and called it recognition. Dark theme had the same defect in reverse. The accent is now only ever a fill: the left rule (where Discord actually puts it, which is what the previous top strip was asked about), the dot, the command token, the filled value chip, the aura. Where text sits on that fill the foreground is solved instead — and unlike the old approach that one cannot fail: solve the crossover where black and white are equally bad and it sits at relative luminance 0.1791, where the better of the two still measures 4.58:1. Measured on the rendered page in light theme, /patch notes is now true rgb(242,194,48) at 12.53:1.

The six "colourless" commands became the most alive ones. Six commands derive an accent per render instead of carrying a fixed one, and that fact was drawn as a hollow outlined dot, which reads as unfinished rather than as true. utils/loadoutRender.js has carried a MP_CATEGORY_ACCENT map all along — seven real weapon-category colours the bot genuinely answers in — so the page now reads it at build time: the derived six wear one quiet grey rather than a hollow outline, and /gunsmiths list re-tints the entire panel to the category you pick, because that is exactly what the bot will do. Choose LMG and the panel turns Grape Purple #845EC2. The page demonstrates its own sentence instead of asserting it, and the palette went from eight colours to fifteen.

Searching "loadout" returned one of the three loadout commands. The index matched the command, its purpose, its option names and its choice labels — everything the bot declares, none of which contains the word a player types. /gunsmiths list and /dmz are entirely about loadouts and matched nothing. Every command now carries a hand-written keyword vocabulary, gated by an oracle of real queries that asserts an exact set rather than a superset, because a search returning everything fails as badly as one returning nothing.

Three pieces of chrome came off this page. The "On this page" accordion no longer renders — the rail already is that navigation, and stacking both cost 107px above the fold under a 54px bar. The trademark disclaimer is gone (pageFoot() already had the variant; two other templates use it): it earns its place under a legal instrument and is noise under a command reference. And the stage's min-height:60vh, which existed to stop the footer moving, was buying that with a screenful of void under every short panel.

Then a third review, and the honest finding is that several of its defects were mine from the second. Adding Discord's own registered option description as "the help layer" did not remove the hand-written sentence it superseded, so an option printed its description three times — Discord's, then a near-identical hand-written one, then that one again in the free-text branch. The per-option prose layer is now deleted outright: Discord's description is what the client shows a reader a second later, so one authoritative sentence replaces three that agreed. The IN DISCORD line went with it — it restated the purpose line directly above it — and each command now carries up to three facts a reader could not guess instead: that weapon search matches partial words and updates live, that a blank style returns all nine formats, that /help answers privately by default.

visibility is a real option again, and the page was calling a lie truth. It had been filtered out of the option list and described in prose, and because the filter ran before the empty-check, /invite rendered "No options — just run it." while its one option sat in the footnote three lines below. It is a selectable option like any other and is now drawn as one.

Every command card was loading with its own heading cut off. scroll-margin-top had zero occurrences in the file — the rewrite dropped it — so every fragment jump parked the panel under a 54px fixed bar plus a sticky rail. It fired on all fourteen.

The page now searches the weapon list the bot searches. The site builds with no database, so scripts/exportWeaponIndex.mjs dumps weapon names, keys, categories and build counts into a committed JSON — 68 MP and 7 DMZ weapons — which the page inlines. Typing "hol" finds Holger 26, and an exact match re-tints the whole panel to that weapon's own category colour: AK117 turns it AR Crimson, FENNEC Electric Gold, LOCUS Electric Blue. ⚠️ The artifact is the cost of that choice, so scripts/weaponIndex.test.js fails on a missing, malformed or implausibly small file — including a case proving the plausibility floor can reject the one-row index that the exporter's own first run produced from a wrong field name.

Four of the eleven /gunsmiths list scopes made the card lose all colour. All MP builds, Meta — MP, Meta — DMZ and DMZ have no entry in MP_CATEGORY_ACCENT, so the re-tint fell through to removeProperty. They now take the bot's own MP and DMZ identity colours, read out of commands/manage.js, with the two meta scopes held darker. The rail chip follows the live tint too, rather than staying grey while the card changed.

Copy stopped refusing, and Clear appeared. Disabling Copy while a required option was empty removed a legitimate action — copying the bare command so you can type the rest in Discord. And every token in the line is now a button that opens its own option, the way clicking an option pill in Discord opens its picker.

The landing state leads with the commands, and it behaves differently on a phone. Fourteen full cards — name, purpose, option chips — made the mobile landing 3292px, 4.1 screenfuls, on the device most of these readers use. On mobile the cards collapse to a two-per-row grid of names, so all fourteen are visible at once, which the horizontally-scrolling rail above cannot do; the landing came back to 1934px. The fold threshold that hid five of eleven scopes behind "+5 more" was 6, tuned for a layout that no longer exists; it is 12, and an open slot now spans both grid columns so a fifteen-item list uses the full width instead of one narrow column beside an empty one.

Two accessibility gaps closed with it. Filtering the index changed the list with no status message, so a screen-reader user got no signal that results had narrowed or emptied — there is now a polite role="status" region that is silent at rest and says "2 of 14 match" or names the miss. And a :target panel swap moved the viewport but no focus, so activating a command left the reader on the link while the stage changed behind them; the panels carry tabindex="-1" so the fragment moves focus into them, the same technique the skip link uses on <main>. Verified at a real 375px touch viewport with pointer:coarse actually matching: no horizontal overflow, every control at 44px, and the stage ordered above the index on a phone so a reader who is lost meets the ask index first.

One CSS trap is worth the words, because it fails silently and reads as correct. The sticky command line is position:fixed on a phone, and it was measured at top:1268px in an 812px window — painted, correct in the source, and nowhere anyone could see it. The card containing it animates on arrival, and an animation filling forwards leaves its final keyframe applied as a computed value: a final transform: none computes to the identity matrix, and a transform of any value — identity included — makes its element a containing block for every fixed descendant. Releasing the fill fixed it after the animation but not during, so every command switch threw the line off screen for 300ms. The arrival motion now lives on the heading block and the accent rule, neither of which has a fixed descendant, and the card animates opacity only.

scripts/lib/commandCatalog.js also now mirrors help.js's own detailCommands || staticCommands precedence, added by #154. It changes nothing today — the built catalog is byte-identical either way — but reading only the coarse list would compute gated from an ungated parent, so a future subcommand carrying its own requires would be hidden in /help and published on the website with every gate green. Two new test cases, both verified to fail against the one-list version.

Also closed: .github/workflows/deploy-site.yml did not watch commands/** or the three new modules, so a command rename could have shipped a page that silently disagreed with the bot; dior legal check was found globbing the public/legal/ directory deleted in the 2026-08-05 flattening, checking 2 files instead of 8 (filed cross-project — it lives in a separate repo); and the build's contrast audit only matched :root[data-theme="light"] with quotes, so an unquoted light block was never read at all — widening the matcher took it from 3 variables to 13.

Pre-Release v3.50.0

#158 f3e0303

A small follow-up session picked up two loose ends from the review-remnants plan, neither of them worth their own review-remnants session: a CI-only bug found (but not fixed) during Session 2, and a filed UX question that turned out not to be as open as it looked.

scripts/reflow-comments.mjs's externalCheck() shelled out to node --check /dev/stdin (and bash -n /dev/stdin), which crashes on GitHub Actions' Linux runners with ENOENT on a /proc/<pid>/fd/socket path — Node's /dev/stdin resolution breaks when the underlying fd is a socket rather than a regular pipe, a quirk that's invisible on macOS and only ever fires for a file with a genuinely proposed change. Found live on PR #156's CI run, deliberately not fixed there to avoid scope-creeping a review-remnants PR into the reflow tooling itself. Fixed here with the identified workaround: text now writes to a real temp file (cleaned up in a finally block) instead of being piped through /dev/stdin. 6 new regression cases (27 total, up from 21) cover valid/invalid JS and shell syntax, temp-file cleanup, and a structural guard that no code line references /dev/stdin any more — a revert would fail that test even if syntax checking happened to still work locally.

/help's "no options besides visibility" wording — filed from Session 1 as three inconsistent treatments needing a canonical pick — turned out to be two things, not one, on a closer look: the four single-command categories already use the correct shape (renderCommandBlock()'s per-command header), and the two admin pages' shared-footnote pattern isn't an inconsistency at all — it's Harkirat's own explicit 2026-08-10 decision to stop repeating the Options header per command specifically because it read as overwhelming. Applying "pick one style everywhere" would have silently reverted that. Surfaced before touching anything; folded into a broader /help design pass Harkirat already has planned, rather than treated as a standalone quick pick.

npm test green throughout (full suite). docs:audit clean on this branch's own commits.

Pre-Release v3.49.0

#157 b56d504

The third and last session of the review-remnants plan (local/handoff/review-remnants-plan.md, gitignored), closing finding #56 — the one finding the plan deliberately kept isolated in its own session rather than folding in beside unrelated work, since it directly intersects finding #12's shutdown-race fix.

utils/eventStore.js's SearchTerm upsert was the one write in the event plane bypassing the FLUSH_AT buffer, issuing a standalone updateOne per closed search session. It now goes through a buffered bulkWrite — the same FLUSH_AT/idle-timer/MAX_BUFFER discipline the event buffer already uses — flushed through flushSearchSessions(), the same shutdown call site finding #12 hooked flushEvents() into.

Re-reading finding #12's fix fresh, rather than trusting it by reputation, surfaced a real defect in it: installShutdownFlush() and utils/instanceLock.js's releaseLock both register listeners on the same SIGTERM/SIGINT, and Node invokes every listener for one signal synchronously, back-to-back. flushSearchSessions()/flushEvents() splice their buffers the instant they're called — so whichever listener ran SECOND always found the buffers already drained by the first and resolved via pure microtasks, calling process.exit() before the first listener's real, macrotask-bound Mongo write could land. Finding #12 closed the race only for the narrower pre-ClientReady window where releaseLock is the sole listener — not the realistic post-ClientReady case where both coexist. Fixed by memoizing the shutdown flush into one shared promise, flushAllForShutdown(), that every listener on the signal now awaits instead of each independently re-invoking flush functions that are individually idempotent-but-fast-no-op on a second call.

Live-verified against real local dev Mongo, not just npm test — a real process shutdown is structurally outside what a unit test can exercise. A disposable harness (not committed) reproduced the pre-memoization race directly: a real SIGTERM with two independent listeners silently dropped the buffered write, confirmed absent via mongosh. The shipped fix landed the write across 4 repeated real SIGTERM runs against the actual acquireInstanceLock()/installShutdownFlush() code paths. 4 new pure-logic cases cover the buffered op shape, the FLUSH_AT auto-trigger, and the memoization itself (scripts/eventStore.test.js, 27 cases total, up from 23).

npm test green throughout (full suite). This closes the review-remnants plan except for finding #9 (AnalyticsEvent TTL), which stays a deliberately out-of-scope conditional item until mid-September 2026 per the already-settled retention decision.

The filed entry says so in its own preamble so the next reader does not re-derive it.

Pre-Release v3.45.0

#153 88afe83

A /code-review max pass over the entire v3-pre-release branch (47 commits, 319 files, 21,077 added / 12,219 removed lines vs main) surfaced 68 findings — nine ship-blockers, dozens of smaller correctness bugs, cleanup, and stale docs. This release applies 61 of them directly (14 in a first pass covering the ship-blockers and one-line data-integrity fixes, 47 more in a second pass covering the rest); 1 was deliberately left unfixed on an already-settled retention decision, 5 were deliberately skipped as needing a new architectural abstraction rather than a bounded fix, and 1 needed no action. Full report: local/handoff/2026-08-18-v3-pre-release-code-review.md (gitignored); status entry: docs/db-deferred-list.md.

The nine ship-blockers: /gunsmiths list's Copy Code button could hand back a different build's Gunsmith code than the card on screen (fixed by resolving through the same scope-aware chain the card renders from); models/SeasonalData.js's draft.calendar couldn't store isDoubleCP, so Promote to Live silently flattened every staged 2X CP event; /draw calculator rendered the un-doubled CP figure for every 2X pack; 22+ MP categories could make /gunsmiths list's scope-choice registration throw with no try/catch around it, silently skipping ALL command registration; a transient Cloudinary error crashed the /colors Nameplate view via an unbound identifier; three admin-grant confirmations posted publicly instead of ephemerally; /manage's purge-confirm and delete-confirm skipped the per-page permission re-check on the actual destructive step; models/AnalyticsEvent.js had no retention path and would eventually exhaust the free-tier Atlas cluster (left unfixed — see below); and scripts/backupDb.sh, the only backup this database has, aborted silently under set -e before its own error guard could ever print.

Beyond the ship-blockers: a full /manage subsystem dedup pass collapsed 24 duplicated SeasonalData fetch call sites and 3 copy-pasted bulk-delete confirmation scaffolds down to one shared helper each, plus similar consolidation for upsert/removal-by-title logic, the loadout mode↔page-key mapping, export-file replies, and the denial-message string; the instance-lock's startup guard closed a real TOCTOU race with an atomic claim; the roll-up job now re-touches its last-rolled day so a late-arriving event is never permanently uncounted, and fires on ClientReady in addition to the 24h heartbeat interval so a same-day double-deploy can no longer stall it indefinitely; all 41 timezone dropdown labels now derive their DST abbreviation live instead of baking in a fixed one (15 of 41 zones observe DST); and a cluster of Cloudinary/Discord-CDN cache-consistency bugs (a distinguishable error sentinel, a complete rawContext on every memoized entry, an in-flight render de-dup) closes the gap where a transient network blip could re-render and re-post an already-cached design.

Held, not fixed: models/AnalyticsEvent.js's missing TTL (finding #9) — Harkirat already decided 2026-08-16 to defer the retention number until a month of real production fill-rate data exists; re-opening it as a new question would have re-litigated a settled call. Skipped, each needing a new architectural addition rather than a bounded fix in code this session couldn't click-test: the CP-currency/timezone picker's 4 duplicated site-pairs, /help's page-builder rewrite, cpPackages.js's return-value spread (its own test file reads it directly), a new buffer+flush cycle for SearchTerm upserts (would sit on the exact shutdown-race territory this same release just fixed), and a documented-load-bearing-ordering restructure in colorPalette.js's cross-view refresh.

npm test green throughout; two existing tests were updated (not reverted) to match intentional behavior changes rather than the bugs they used to encode: rollupStore.test.js's idempotency case now expects the last-rolled day to be re-touched, and discordCdnAssetIndex.test.js's recovery-happy-path assertion now expects the recovered discordMessageId in the return.

Pre-Release v3.44.0

#152 4e004a5

A deleted Cloudinary resource used to permanently orphan its Discord storage-channel message and force a full re-render + duplicate upload on the next view, even though the exact bytes were still sitting in the channel — the same code that posted the message discarded its id instead of remembering it. Traced during a re-verification of an existing docs/db-deferred-list.md item ("does the grouped-upload path share the single-file path's orphan behavior?"); confirming the claim held wasn't a good enough answer, since the underlying data to do better was already sitting in the same upload response.

Adds a durable, Cloudinary-INDEPENDENT secondary index (models/DiscordCdnAsset.js + utils/discordCdnAssetIndex.js) — one row per rendered design, written alongside every storage-channel upload in BOTH the live per-view path (utils/nameplateWebpCache.js/utils/decorationWebpCache.js) and the bulk script's grouped path (scripts/bulkCacheCollectibles.js), so it survives a later Cloudinary-side deletion untouched. On a Cloudinary cache-miss, the index is checked before treating it as a cold render: if a record exists, the still-live cdn.discordapp.com bytes are re-fetched directly and re-uploaded to Cloudinary at the same public_id, restoring the cache and skipping the render pipeline's single most expensive phase (frame compositing + ffmpeg encode) entirely, then letting the existing palette self-heal re-derive what only Cloudinary ever held. utils/discordCdnStorage.js's two upload functions now return the message id they were silently discarding.

Also fixes an adjacent bug found while wiring this in: healPalette() in both cache modules replaced Cloudinary's context wholesale on every palette heal (a Cloudinary api.update context write replaces the whole map), silently wiping render_source/catalog metadata each time — now merges onto the previously-read context instead of rebuilding it from scratch.

utils/discordCdnAssetIndex.test.js (11 cases covering the index and every recovery branch, including a partial-success-after-failure case) added to npm test. docs/db-deferred-list.md's two related entries updated to describe the shipped fix rather than the accepted workaround.

Pre-Release v3.42.0

#150 0e8a990
  • node --watch restarts no longer lose the race with the instance lock. The dev-bot workflow (node --watch --env-file=.env.dev index.js) could kill the bot for the rest of a session: a restart kills the old process before its async Mongo lock release lands, so the new process reads a heartbeat that still looks fresh and wrongly refuses to start — silently, with the terminal still looking healthy. utils/instanceLock.js's acquireInstanceLock now also checks whether the lock's pid is still alive on this host (process.kill(pid, 0)) before honoring a fresh heartbeat; cross-host locking (a local Mac vs. the prod VM) is untouched, since a remote pid can't be probed this way. Verified live: a genuine boot, a real concurrent-instance refusal (the guard still works), four rapid --watch restarts (zero false refusals, previously the exact failure), and the dead-pid-stale-lock edge case (an unclean exit now restarts instantly instead of waiting out the 30s staleness window).
  • NOTICE now credits all 11 Flaticon icon authors, in Flaticon's required attribution format (its free tier requires attribution). 10 of 11 were verified live one-by-one via a real browser (Flaticon blocks bot fetches outright); customicondesign_1's actual URL slug turned out to be customicondesign-1 — hyphenated, despite the underscore in its own display name — which a naive derivation would have gotten wrong. The 11th, Magnific, is credited by name with no author link: Flaticon's own parent company recently renamed itself Freepik → Magnific too, which broke that individual author's profile URL on Flaticon's end.

Pre-Release v3.41.0

#149 ce87e72

/invite rebuilt from Harkirat's own mockup (local/invite_ui.json). Two structural simplifications came out of it. The two explicit guild/user buttons collapse to one Invite button on the bare chooser URL, letting Discord's own Add App picker offer whichever install types the application has enabled — the platform does the branching, so the panel cannot drift from the Developer Portal's settings. And the fenced share block becomes a real Share Link button, whose handler replies with the raw discord.com/oauth2 URL and nothing else: Discord unfurls its own authorization links into an app card, and a bare body makes "copy text" yield exactly the link.

Five values in that mockup were resolved rather than copied, because it was built live on the dev bot. The client_id and the </help:…> mention id were the dev application's; flags: 36864 carried SUPPRESS_NOTIFICATIONS on top of Components V2; the custom_id was mockup-generated. The one that would have broken silently in production was the mascot: a signed cdn.discordapp.com attachment URL whose ex=/is=/hm= params expire within about a day — the exact failure this repo already fixed by re-hosting that asset, reintroduced by hand.

The mascot now loads 95% smaller, and the fix was not the one asked for. Harkirat asked whether PR #146's Cloudinary memoization could speed the mascot up. It cannot: that fix memoizes cloudinary.api.resource() Admin API lookups (138–470ms each) for runtime-resolved public_ids, and this URL is a constant — there is no lookup, so that cost is already zero. The real cost was bytes: a 2048×2048 source delivered with only f_auto,q_auto into an ~80-point thumbnail. Measured against the live CDN: 266,911 → 13,601 bytes at w_256, 94.9% smaller (w_160 = 7,143, w_128 = 5,450, recorded as the further levers). ⚠️ That figure is the origin fetch; Discord serves message images through its own caching media proxy, so the win is on cold fetch and proxy ingest rather than a measured client-side render time. The URL also moves into new utils/brandAssets.js — it was a duplicate literal in commands/help.js and commands/invite.js, and the transform would otherwise have landed on one copy and left the other slow, invisibly.

A skipExpiry opt-out at the sendV2Payload boundary, defaulting off. Share Link is a real custom_id button, which normally re-arms the 10-minute idle-disable for the whole container — greying it out beside a still-live Invite link on exactly the public post the command exists to leave behind. The bar for this flag is "nothing on this panel can go stale", not "losing it is inconvenient"; /invite qualifies structurally, since its handler answers with its own fresh token.

/invite has no "Show Everyone" button, by decision — Harkirat, on reviewing it: "i don't actually want the show everyone button for it. they can just send the command again publicly." The command already defaults to public and carries its own Share Link, so a third route to publishing it is redundant; /help dropped the same button on the same reasoning.

It also closed a real bug, which is why it had already gone. Auditing this branch found that the "Show Everyone" path defeated the new opt-out: handlers/share.js builds the public copy and sends it through sendV2Payload itself, without the flag — so a shared /invite armed the timer after all, and its Share Link greyed out ten minutes later on precisely the public post the command exists to leave behind. That shipped live in v3.40.0. Threading the flag through was rejected (share.js has only the message JSON, so it would need its own table of exempt commands — a second copy of the decision) and so was always-skipping there (a shared /settings panel genuinely should expire). ⚠️ The bug later being solved some other way is not a reason to restore the button — the decision above stands on its own.

Staleness found and fixed: .claude/rules/interaction-router.md's handler roster listed alerts and audit — both retired the previous day — while omitting bot, drawCalc (never listed) and invite. Two removals and two additions cancelled out, so its "Fourteen subsystems" count stayed accidentally correct while a fifth of the list was false. The numeral is gone; the roster is now defined as whatever handlers/*.js contains.

The whole result is cached for 60s and the module never throws past its own boundary — a GCP outage degrades the Health page to a plain-language line, not a crash.

Roll-ups — one document per (day, command, subcommand). models/AnalyticsRollup.js/RollupState.js + utils/rollupStore.js. Rides the existing daily heartbeat in bot/lifecycle.js rather than adding a second scheduler; catchUpRollups() is a full recompute-and-upsert per day, so it's safe to re-run and catches up any gap left by downtime, bounded to CATCH_UP_WINDOW_DAYS (14) so a very stale resume point doesn't re-roll an unbounded backlog. Two decisions the frozen spec left explicitly open, resolved here: the day key is UTC and includes the year ('2026-08-16', not alertId/changeId's year-less 'Aug16' — those retain for 30d/180d and can never see two Aug 16ths, a roll-up kept indefinitely can); and distinctUsers stores the day's bounded hash set (userHashes, cap 5,000) so a multi-day distinct-user figure can be a real set union — past the cap, distinctUsersExact flips false and the array is dropped rather than kept partial, since a partial set unioned with another day's would silently undercount.
